title: 5.29.14 Convergence of potentials and measures
text: For quasi-continuous obstacles, a decreasing lower semicontinuous approximation keeps the original bounds and confines the error to sets of vanishing capacity. Lemma 5.29.15 . DF96BD63B553 Every bounded quasi-continuous function $f$ on $X$ admits bounded lower semicontinuous functions $f_ j$ with common bounds such that $f_ j\downarrow f$ quasi-everywhere and $f_ j\to f$ in capacity. Proof. Choose open sets $O_ j$ of capacity at most $2^{-j}$ such that the restriction of $f$ to $X\setminus O_ j$ is continuous, and set $G_ j=\bigcup _{k\geq j}O_ k$. Then the sets $G_ j$ decrease, their capacities tend to zero, and $f$ is continuous on the closed complement of each $G_ j$. Choose $M\geq \sup _ Xf$ and define \[  f_ j=f\  \hbox{on }X\setminus G_ j,\qquad f_ j=M\  \hbox{on }G_ j.  \] At a boundary point of $G_ j$, the values of $f_ j$ on the closed complement tend to the value of $f$ there, while the values inside $G_ j$ are at least that value. Thus $f_ j$ is lower semicontinuous. The functions $f_ j$ decrease to $f$ outside $\bigcap _ jG_ j$, a set of capacity zero. Since $f_ j-f$ is supported in $G_ j$, they also converge to $f$ in capacity. $\square$ Uniform bounds on potentials give a common capacity bound for their mixed measures. Lemma 5.29.16 . F56E1BEB2997 Let $A\geq 0$ and let $0\leq k\leq n$ be an integer. There is a constant $C_ A$ such that all the positive mixed measures \[  \omega _{v_1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \omega _{v_ k}\wedge \omega ^{n-k}, \qquad v_ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega ), \quad \| v_ i\| _\infty \leq A,  \] are bounded above on Borel sets by $C_ A\operatorname {Cap}_\omega $. In particular, their total masses are uniformly bounded. If uniformly bounded functions tend to zero in capacity, then their integrals against these measures tend to zero uniformly in the $v_ i$. Proof. Translate the $v_ i$ so that $0\leq v_ i\leq 2A$, and put $q=(v_1+\cdots +v_ k)/B$, where $B\geq \max \{ 2k,2kA,1\} $. Then $0\leq q\leq 1$ and \[  \omega _ q=B^{-1}\sum _{i=1}^ k\omega _{v_ i}+(1-k/B)\omega ,  \] where all coefficients are positive. Expanding $\omega _ q^ n$ shows that the given mixed product is bounded by a constant multiple of $\omega _ q^ n$, and the definition of capacity proves the first claim. The case $k=0$ follows by testing with $v=0$. For a bounded function $z$, split its integral into the parts over $\{ |z|>t\} $ and over its complement; first use convergence in capacity for fixed $t>0$, and then let $t\downarrow 0$. $\square$ The same control applies to the total variation of a product formed with a different smooth background. Lemma 5.29.17 . 7EE2FAA017DE Let $\Omega $ be a Hermitian form and $\theta $ a smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Suppose that $\Omega $-plurisubharmonic functions $v_ j$ have common finite upper and lower bounds and decrease to $v$. Then the signed measures \[  \nu _ j=(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)^ n  \] converge to $(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n$ against every fixed bounded quasi-continuous function. Their total variations are bounded, uniformly in $j$, by a constant multiple of the local capacity on the balls of a fixed finite cover. Proof. On a relatively compact coordinate ball, choose a fixed quadratic function $q$ such that the functions $v_ j+q$ are plurisubharmonic; they still have common bounds. Expand \[  (\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)^ n =\sum _{\ell =0}^ n\binom n\ell \bigl (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v_ j+q)\bigr )^\ell \wedge (\theta -\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q)^{n-\ell }.  \] The absolute value of the $\ell $-th summand is bounded by a fixed constant times \[  \bigl (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v_ j+q)\bigr )^\ell \wedge \kappa _0^{n-\ell },  \] where $\kappa _0$ is a fixed positive Euclidean form. This positive mixed measure is bounded, uniformly in $j$, by a constant times the local capacity: add a fixed strictly plurisubharmonic quadratic function to $v_ j+q$, expand the top power of its Hessian, and rescale its uniformly bounded range into $[0,1]$ to apply the definition of capacity. This also covers $\ell =0$. Summing over a finite cover gives the asserted control of the total variations. The ordinary decreasing continuity of Bedford–Taylor products gives weak convergence term by term. For a bounded quasi-continuous coefficient, remove an open set of small capacity and extend the restriction of the coefficient to the compact complement to a continuous function on $X$. The variation bound controls the resulting error uniformly for the sequence and its limit, and letting the capacity of the removed set tend to zero proves the assertion. $\square$ A finite non-pluripolar measure is uniformly absolutely continuous with respect to capacity, although it need not be bounded by a power of the capacity. Lemma 5.29.18 . D0C7DB81F772 Let $\mu $ be a finite non-pluripolar Borel measure on $X$. Then \[  \lim _{\delta \downarrow 0}\sup \{ \mu (E):E\text{ Borel}, \operatorname {Cap}_\omega (E)\leq \delta \} =0.  \] Consequently, convergence in capacity implies convergence in $\mu $-measure. Proof. If the first assertion failed, there would be $\epsilon >0$ and Borel sets $E_ j$ of capacity at most $2^{-j}$ with $\mu (E_ j)\geq \epsilon $. By countable subadditivity of capacity, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_\omega \left(\limsup _ j E_ j\right)=0.  \] Hence $\limsup _ jE_ j$ is pluripolar and has $\mu $-measure zero. On the other hand, since $\mu $ is finite, continuity from above applied to the sets $\bigcup _{k\geq j}E_ k$ shows that $\limsup _ jE_ j$ has measure at least $\epsilon $, a contradiction. If $u_ j\to u$ in capacity, applying the first assertion to the sets $\{ |u_ j-u|>\delta \} $ gives the consequence. $\square$ Lemma 5.29.19 . 505602F4CB54 Let $u_ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Suppose either that $u_ j$ decreases to a function $u\not\equiv -\infty $, or that $u_ j$ increases, the sequence is uniformly bounded above, and $u=(\lim _ j u_ j)^*$. Then $u_ j\to u$ in capacity. Proof. In the decreasing case $u$ is a common lower bound for the sequence and its limit; in the increasing case $u_1$ is one. Choose a Hermitian form $\Omega \geq \theta $ and truncate all functions at $-T$. The truncations are bounded, monotone and $\Omega $-plurisubharmonic, so the convergence in capacity of locally bounded monotone sequences, recalled in section 5.27 , applies to them on the balls of a finite cover. By quasi-continuity of the common lower bound, there is an open set of arbitrarily small capacity containing its pole set such that the restriction of the lower bound to the compact complement is continuous. There it is finite and hence bounded below, so the capacity of the sublevel set of the lower bound at height $-T$ tends to zero as $T\to \infty $. Since the functions agree with their truncations outside this sublevel set, letting $T\to \infty $ proves the lemma. $\square$ A fixed bounded reference potential also controls a mixed trace in which one normalized potential varies. Lemma 5.29.20 . 31C5645526CA Let $\theta \geq 0$, and fix a bounded $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. There is a constant $C_\psi $ such that \[  \int _ X\theta _ v\wedge \theta _\psi ^{n-1}\leq C_\psi  \] for every bounded $v\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\sup _ Xv=0$. Proof. For $n=1$, Stokes' theorem gives $\int _ X\theta _ v=\int _ X\theta $, so assume $n\geq 2$. Choose a fixed Hermitian form $\Omega \geq \theta $. All currents on the left-hand side are positive, and $\Omega _\psi \geq \theta _\psi $. Hence Stokes' theorem for bounded potentials gives \[  \int _ X\theta _ v\wedge \theta _\psi ^{n-1} \leq \int _ X\theta \wedge \Omega _\psi ^{n-1} +\int _ Xv\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\Omega _\psi ^{n-1}).  \] The first term on the right is bounded independently of $v$. To estimate the second, differentiate: \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\Omega _\psi ^{n-1}) =(n-1)\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Omega \wedge \Omega _\psi ^{n-2} +(n-1)(n-2)\mathrm{d}\Omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\Omega \wedge \Omega _\psi ^{n-3},  \] where the second term is absent for $n=2$. Since $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Omega $ and $\mathrm d\Omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\Omega $ are smooth forms, the absolute values of these terms are bounded by fixed multiples of the positive measures $\Omega ^2\wedge \Omega _\psi ^{n-2}$ and $\Omega ^3\wedge \Omega _\psi ^{n-3}$. The weighted local Chern–Levine–Nirenberg inequality of section 5.27 bounds the integrals of $|v|$ against these measures. Indeed, on each larger coordinate ball, add fixed smooth corrections to $v$ and $\psi $, shift the corrected $v$ so that it becomes negative, expand in the corrected positive Hessian of $\psi $, and apply that inequality on a smaller ball. The resulting bound is \[  C(1+\| \psi \| _\infty )^ n(1+\| v\| _{L^1(X)}).  \] By theorem 5.25.2 , normalized $\theta $-plurisubharmonic functions have uniformly bounded $L^1$ norms, and summing the local bounds proves the assertion. $\square$

title: 5.29.21 Vanishing area on curves
text: On a compact curve, the integral of the background is the total mass of every curvature current. When this integral vanishes, positivity forces the current to vanish. Normalized compactness and the local estimate of capacity by total variation make this uniqueness stable as the area tends to zero. Throughout this subsection, $Y$ is a compact connected Riemann surface and $\eta $ is a smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $Y$ with $\int _ Y\eta =1$, which we use for $L^1$ norms and for the capacity $\operatorname {Cap}_\eta $ on $Y$. Lemma 5.29.22 . E8D07C38BC7C For a smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\sigma $ on $Y$, put $A=\int _ Y\sigma $. There is a smooth real function $h$ with $\sigma =A\eta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h$. The class $\mathrm{PSH}(Y,\sigma )$ is nonempty if and only if $A\geq 0$. If $A=0$, it consists of the functions $-h+c$, $c\in \mathbb R$, and its unique member with supremum zero is $u_\sigma =-h+\min _ Yh$. Proof. The smooth form $\sigma -A\eta $ has integral zero, so the Poisson equation on the compact connected surface $Y$ has a smooth solution $h$, unique up to an additive constant. If $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(Y,\sigma )$, positivity and Stokes' theorem give \[  0\leq (\sigma +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)(Y)=A.  \] Conversely, $\sigma +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(-h)=A\eta $, so $-h\in \mathrm{PSH}(Y,\sigma )$ when $A\geq 0$. If $A=0$, every positive curvature measure has total mass zero and therefore vanishes. Thus $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u+h)=0$ for every $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(Y,\sigma )$, and elliptic regularity and the uniqueness of harmonic functions on $Y$ show that $u+h$ is constant. Normalizing the supremum gives the stated formula. $\square$ Theorem 5.29.23 . FD7A4AE0DAC6 Let $\sigma _ j$ be smooth real $(1,1)$-forms on $Y$ that converge uniformly to a smooth form $\sigma _0$, and suppose that \[  A_ j=\int _ Y\sigma _ j\geq 0,\qquad \int _ Y\sigma _0=0.  \] Let $u_0$ be the normalized $\sigma _0$-plurisubharmonic potential of lemma 5.29.22 . Then, for every $t>0$, \[  \begin{aligned}  \sup _{u\in \mathrm{PSH}(Y,\sigma _ j),\  \sup _ Yu=0}\| u-u_0\| _{L^1(Y)}& \longrightarrow 0,\\  \sup _{u\in \mathrm{PSH}(Y,\sigma _ j),\  \sup _ Yu=0} \operatorname {Cap}_\eta (\{ |u-u_0|>t\} )& \longrightarrow 0. \end{aligned}  \] Moreover, the curvature measures $\sigma _ j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ of these potentials tend to zero in total variation, uniformly in $u$, since each has total variation $A_ j$. Proof. Choose $C>0$ with $\sigma _ j\leq C\eta $ for every $j$. Every sequence of normalized $\sigma _ j$-plurisubharmonic functions then lies in the compact family of normalized $C\eta $-plurisubharmonic functions of theorem 5.25.2 . Every $L^1$ limit $u$ of a subsequence is normalized and, by passing to the limit in the sense of distributions, satisfies $\sigma _0+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\geq 0$. The preceding lemma gives $u=u_0$. If the first uniform limit failed, a sequence violating it would have a subsequence converging to this same limit, a contradiction. For a potential $u$ in the $j$-th normalized family, put $T=\sigma _ j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$. Positivity and Stokes' theorem give $\| T\| _{\mathrm{TV}}=A_ j$, and $A_ j\to \int _ Y\sigma _0=0$. Since $\sigma _0+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_0=0$, \[  \| \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u-u_0)\| _{\mathrm{TV}} \leq A_ j+\| \sigma _ j-\sigma _0\| _{\mathrm{TV}}\longrightarrow 0  \] uniformly over that family. Apply lemma 5.27.11 on a fixed finite cover of $Y$ by concentric coordinate disks. The first limit and the bound above make each local capacity tend to zero uniformly, and the comparison between local and global capacity at the beginning of this section proves the second limit. The identity $\| T\| _{\mathrm{TV}}=A_ j$ proves the final assertion. $\square$

title: Theorem 5.29.23
text: Theorem 5.29.23 . FD7A4AE0DAC6 Let $\sigma _ j$ be smooth real $(1,1)$-forms on $Y$ that converge uniformly to a smooth form $\sigma _0$, and suppose that \[  A_ j=\int _ Y\sigma _ j\geq 0,\qquad \int _ Y\sigma _0=0.  \] Let $u_0$ be the normalized $\sigma _0$-plurisubharmonic potential of lemma 5.29.22 . Proof. Choose $C>0$ with $\sigma _ j\leq C\eta $ for every $j$. The first limit and the bound above make each local capacity tend to zero uniformly, and the comparison between local and global capacity at the beginning of this section proves the second limit. The identity $\| T\| _{\mathrm{TV}}=A_ j$ proves the final assertion. $\square$

title: 5.30 Comparing local regularizations
text: To glue local convolutions, we need them to agree on overlaps up to an error tending uniformly to zero. A bounded plurisubharmonic function need not be continuous, so this comparison cannot come from uniform convergence to the original function. Instead, the logarithmic convexity of its suprema over balls controls both the change of scale and the change of coordinates. Let $U\subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a domain and $u$ a bounded plurisubharmonic function on $U$. For $z$ in a fixed relatively compact subset of $U$ and small $\delta >0$, put \[  S_\delta u(z)=\sup _{|\zeta -z|\leq \delta }u(\zeta ),\qquad A_\delta u(z)=\fint _{|\zeta -z|=\delta }u(\zeta )\, \mathrm{d}\sigma (\zeta ), \qquad u_\delta =u*\rho _\delta ,  \] where $\mathrm{d}\sigma $ is the Euclidean surface measure and $\rho $ is a smooth nonnegative radial mollifier of integral one, supported in the unit ball, with $\rho _\delta (\zeta )=\delta ^{-2n}\rho (\zeta /\delta )$. All balls below lie in a fixed larger relatively compact subset of $U$, and $B$ denotes a bound for the oscillation of $u$ on that subset. Lemma 5.30.1 . 2319B6057130 For each fixed $A>1$, \[  S_{A\delta }u-S_\delta u\longrightarrow 0, \qquad S_\delta u-u_\delta \longrightarrow 0  \] uniformly on compact subsets as $\delta \downarrow 0$. Proof. The maximum of a plurisubharmonic function over concentric balls is a convex function of the logarithm of the radius. This follows by restricting to each complex line through the center and comparing, on an annulus, with the harmonic function that is affine in $\log |\zeta |$. Fix a radius $r>A\delta $ for which all the balls of radius $r$ about points of the given compact set lie in the larger subset. Comparing secant slopes of this convex function between $\log \delta $, $\log (A\delta )$ and $\log r$ gives 4BCD629A10F1 5.30.2 \begin{equation}  0\leq S_{A\delta }u-S_\delta u \leq \frac{B\log A}{\log (r/\delta )}, \end{equation} which proves the first assertion. To compare the maximum with the spherical mean, we use the Poisson kernel in real dimension $2n$. For a point at distance at most $\delta /2$ from the center, the normalized Poisson kernel of the ball of radius $\delta $ is bounded below by a positive dimensional constant $c_ n$. Since $u$ is bounded above by $S_\delta u$ and by its harmonic extension from the sphere of radius $\delta $, we obtain \[  S_\delta u-S_{\delta /2}u \geq c_ n(S_\delta u-A_\delta u).  \] These inequalities hold for bounded plurisubharmonic functions by local smoothing followed by a decreasing limit. By ( 5.30.2 ), $S_\delta u-A_\delta u$ therefore tends uniformly to zero. For $0<t\leq 1$, the spherical mean is increasing in the radius, and \[  0\leq A_\delta u-A_{t\delta }u \leq (S_\delta u-S_{t\delta }u) +(S_{t\delta }u-A_{t\delta }u).  \] By logarithmic convexity, the first term is at most $B\log (1/t)/\log (r/(t\delta ))$, and by the preceding estimate the second is at most $C_ nB/\log (r/(t\delta ))$. Write the radial convolution as an average of the spherical means $A_{t\delta }u$ with respect to the probability density $\widehat\rho (t)=|\mathbb S^{2n-1}|t^{2n-1}\rho (t)$ on $[0,1]$, where $\rho (t)$ denotes the value of $\rho $ at radius $t$. Since $\int _0^1(1+\log (1/t))\widehat\rho (t)\, \mathrm{d}t<\infty $, integration gives \[  0\leq A_\delta u-u_\delta \leq \frac{C_{n,\rho }B}{\log (r/\delta )}.  \] Combining the two comparisons proves the second assertion. $\square$ Corollary 5.30.3 . ACA94F989A1E Let $U,V\subset \mathbb C^ n$ be domains, let $F:U\to V$ be biholomorphic, and let $u$ be bounded and plurisubharmonic on $U$. Then \[  u_\delta -\bigl ((u\circ F^{-1})*\rho _\delta \bigr )\circ F  \] tends locally uniformly to zero as $\delta \downarrow 0$. Proof. On a compact subset, $F$ and its inverse have uniformly bounded first derivatives. Thus, for a fixed $A>1$, the inverse image under $F$ of the ball of radius $\delta $ about $F(z)$ lies between the balls about $z$ of radii $\delta /A$ and $A\delta $. Consequently, $S_\delta (u\circ F^{-1})(F(z))$ and $S_\delta u(z)$ both lie between $S_{\delta /A}u(z)$ and $S_{A\delta }u(z)$, and the first assertion of lemma 5.30.1 shows that their difference tends to zero uniformly. The second assertion of the lemma, applied to $u$ and to $u\circ F^{-1}$, compares each of the two convolutions with the corresponding supremum regularization. $\square$

section: 5.31 Gluing with a small curvature error
text: The overlap estimate allows local regularizations to be glued by a regularized maximum. Small corrections near the boundary of each chart make the corresponding local branch irrelevant there, while convexity of the regularized maximum preserves a common lower curvature bound. The curvature error is measured by the Hermitian form $\omega $. For an integer $N\geq 1$, choose independent real random variables $Z_1,\ldots ,Z_ N$ with a common smooth even probability density supported in $[-1,1]$, and define \[  M_\tau (t_1,\ldots ,t_ N) =\mathbb E\max _ i(t_ i+\tau Z_ i)\quad (\tau >0).  \] As a convolution, $M_\tau $ is smooth. It is convex and increasing in every argument, and, with $\mathbf1=(1,\ldots ,1)$, it satisfies \[  \max _ i t_ i\leq M_\tau (t)\leq \max _ i t_ i+\tau , \qquad M_\tau (t+c\mathbf1)=M_\tau (t)+c  \] for $t\in \mathbb R^ N$ and $c\in \mathbb R$. If $t_ i<\max _{j\ne i}t_ j-2\tau $, then the $i$-th argument can be removed without changing the value. Moreover, $M_\tau (t)$ is nondecreasing in $\tau $, because it is a convex even function of $\tau $, the distribution of each $Z_ i$ being symmetric. The second identity expresses invariance under translations. If smooth real functions $f_ i$, $1\leq i\leq N$, satisfy $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_ i\geq -\gamma $ for a common smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\gamma $, then 38E79A7BB294 5.31.1 \begin{equation}  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}M_\tau (f_1,\ldots ,f_ N)\geq -\gamma . \end{equation} Indeed, in the chain rule the first partial derivatives of $M_\tau $ are nonnegative and, by the translation identity, sum to one, while the real Hessian of the convex function $M_\tau $ contributes a semipositive $(1,1)$-form. Proposition 5.31.2 . 752BA1321BFA Let $\theta $ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form, let $\omega $ be a Hermitian form, and let $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cap L^\infty (X)$. There are smooth functions $v_ j$ and positive numbers $\varepsilon _ j\downarrow 0$ such that \[  v_ j\downarrow u,\qquad \theta +\varepsilon _ j\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j\geq 0.  \] Proof. For fixed $\epsilon >0$, we first glue the local convolutions of $u$ by a regularized maximum, obtaining smooth functions that decrease to $u$ and have curvature error $2\epsilon \omega $; a diagonal sequence then proves the proposition. Step 1: local regularizations. Fix $\epsilon >0$. By continuity of $\theta $, we can choose finitely many nested coordinate neighborhoods $V_ i\Subset W_ i\Subset U_ i$, with the $V_ i$ covering $X$, and smooth quadratic functions $r_ i$ such that \[  0\leq \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}r_ i-\theta \leq \epsilon \omega \quad \hbox{on }U_ i.  \] To do so, freeze the coefficients of $\theta $ at the center of a chart, add a small positive constant form, and shrink the coordinate neighborhood. Then $p_ i=u+r_ i$ is a bounded plurisubharmonic function on $U_ i$; let $p_{i,\delta }$ be its convolution in the coordinates of $U_ i$. On an overlap, express both $p_ i$ and $p_ j$ in the coordinates of $U_ j$. Their difference is the smooth function $r_ i-r_ j$, so the difference of their convolutions in these coordinates tends uniformly to $r_ i-r_ j$. By corollary 5.30.3 , changing the coordinates in which $p_ i$ is convolved introduces another uniformly vanishing error. Thus, on the intersections of the closures of the $W_ i$, BF9EF9467EBB 5.31.3 \begin{equation}  (p_{i,\delta }-r_ i)-(p_{j,\delta }-r_ j)\longrightarrow 0 \quad \hbox{uniformly}. \end{equation} Step 2: gluing. Choose functions $\eta _ i\in C^\infty (U_ i,[-1,0])$ that vanish on $V_ i$ and equal $-1$ near the boundary of $W_ i$, and a constant $C\geq 1$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\eta _ i\geq -C\omega $. The cover, the functions $r_ i,\eta _ i$ and the constant $C$ may depend on $\epsilon $; they are fixed while $\delta $ tends to zero. Set \[  f_{i,\delta }=p_{i,\delta }-r_ i+(\epsilon /C)\eta _ i \quad \hbox{on }W_ i.  \] Each of these functions satisfies $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_{i,\delta }\geq -\theta -2\epsilon \omega $. Every boundary point of $W_ i$ lies in some $V_ j$, and there $\eta _ j=0$ while $\eta _ i=-1$. By ( 5.31.3 ), for all small $\delta $, \[  f_{i,\delta }<f_{j,\delta }-\epsilon /(2C)  \] on a neighborhood of that boundary point. Since the cover is finite, this separation holds uniformly. Let $\tau (\delta )\downarrow 0$ as $\delta \downarrow 0$, with $\tau (\delta )<\epsilon /(8C)$, and define the value at each point as the regularized maximum $M_{\tau (\delta )}$ of the functions $f_{i,\delta }$ for those $i$ with the point in $W_ i$. A branch disappears only near the boundary of its $W_ i$, where it lies below another branch by more than $2\tau $. By the removal property of $M_\tau $, these local formulas therefore define a global smooth function $\psi _{\epsilon ,\delta }$, and ( 5.31.1 ) gives \[  \theta +2\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _{\epsilon ,\delta }\geq 0.  \] At every point there is a branch with $\eta _ i=0$, and $p_{i,\delta }\geq p_ i$; hence $\psi _{\epsilon ,\delta }\geq u$. For fixed $\epsilon $, the local convolutions decrease with $\delta $, and the regularized maximum decreases when both its arguments and $\tau $ decrease. Its pointwise limit is \[  \max _{i:x\in W_ i}\bigl (u(x)+(\epsilon /C)\eta _ i(x)\bigr )=u(x).  \] Thus $\psi _{\epsilon ,\delta }\downarrow u$ as $\delta \downarrow 0$, and also in $L^1$. Step 3: a diagonal sequence. Take $\epsilon _ j\downarrow 0$ and put $v_ j=\psi _{\epsilon _ j,\delta _ j}+2^{-j}$, where $\delta _ j$ is chosen so small that \[  \| \psi _{\epsilon _ j,\delta _ j}-u\| _{L^1}\leq 2^{-j}, \qquad v_ j<v_{j-1}\quad (j\geq 2).  \] The second requirement can be met because $v_{j-1}\geq u+2^{-j+1}$. Indeed, as $\delta \downarrow 0$, the continuous functions $\psi _{\epsilon _ j,\delta }+2^{-j}-v_{j-1}$ decrease pointwise to a function bounded above by $-2^{-j}$. Their sets of nonnegative values are decreasing compact sets with empty intersection, so one of them is empty. The resulting sequence $(v_ j)$ decreases, converges to $u$ in $L^1$, and stays above $u$. Its pointwise limit is $(\theta +2\epsilon _ k\omega )$-plurisubharmonic for every $k$, hence $\theta $-plurisubharmonic, and it equals $u$ almost everywhere; by lemma 5.24.3 , it equals $u$ everywhere. Taking $\varepsilon _ j=2\epsilon _ j$ proves the proposition. $\square$

section: 5.32 Regularization in a fixed Hermitian background
text: For $\theta =\omega $, rescaling the approximants absorbs the curvature error into the positive background. Subtracting a constant first makes the approximants negative, so that this rescaling preserves their decreasing order. Theorem 5.32.1 . 240BA0465940 For every $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )\cap L^\infty (X)$, there are smooth functions $u_ j\downarrow u$ such that \[  \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j>0.  \] The functions $u_ j$ are uniformly bounded. Proof. Subtracting a constant, we may assume $u\leq -2$. Apply proposition 5.31.2 with $\theta =\omega $, obtaining smooth functions $v_ j\downarrow u$ and positive numbers $\varepsilon _ j\downarrow 0$ with $(1+\varepsilon _ j)\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j\geq 0$. The compact sets $\{ v_ j\geq -1\} $ decrease to the empty set, since $u\leq -2$. After discarding finitely many terms, we may therefore assume $v_ j<0$ everywhere. Put \[  u_ j=\frac{v_ j}{1+2\varepsilon _ j}.  \] Then \[  \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j \geq \frac{\varepsilon _ j}{1+2\varepsilon _ j}\omega >0.  \] Since $v_ j$ is negative and decreases, while the positive denominator decreases to one, $u_ j$ also decreases, and it converges to $u$. Moreover, $u\leq v_ j\leq u_ j\leq u_1$, which gives uniform boundedness. Adding back the subtracted constant proves the theorem. $\square$ This regularization provides the approximation used for products and mass in section 13.14 . For an arbitrary smooth form $\theta $, proposition 5.31.2 only gives approximants whose curvature error tends to zero.

title: 5.33 Singularity type and multiplier ideals
text: There are two natural ways to compare the singularities of quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$. The first asks whether one function is bounded above by the other up to an additive constant; it leads to the ordinary singularity type. The second records only which holomorphic functions are locally square integrable against the weights $\mathrm{e}^{-ku}$, $k>0$; it leads to multiplier ideals. Domination implies the corresponding inclusion of multiplier ideals. A logarithmic pole on a disk shows that a single weight loses information, which is why the second comparison uses all positive weights. Definition 16.7.1 . 3E4D57445698 Let $u,v$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$. We write $u\preceq v$ if there is a constant $C\in \mathbb R$ such that $u\leq v+C$ on $X$, and $u\sim v$ if both $u\preceq v$ and $v\preceq u$; in the latter case $u$ and $v$ have the same singularity type . When this has to be distinguished from the multiplier-ideal type introduced below, we speak of the ordinary singularity type , or simply the ordinary type . Thus $u\preceq v$ means that $u$ is at least as singular as $v$. For instance, a quasi-plurisubharmonic function with a logarithmic pole lies below every bounded potential in this order, but not conversely. Proposition 5.33.1 . EFC5ED339FC3 The relation $\preceq $ is a preorder, and $\sim $ is an equivalence relation. If $u$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic and $f$ is a smooth function on $X$, then $u+f\sim u$. In particular, all smooth functions on $X$ have the same singularity type. Proof. Reflexivity follows with $C=0$. If $u\leq v+C$ and $v\leq w+D$, then $u\leq w+C+D$, which proves transitivity. As for every preorder, comparison in both directions defines an equivalence relation. Since $X$ is compact, a smooth function $f$ satisfies $|f|\leq A$ for some constant $A$, and then $u-A\leq u+f\leq u+A$. Taking $u=0$ shows that every smooth function has the singularity type of the constants. $\square$ Some later results require the singularities of a potential to be concentrated on a small closed set. A closed subset $A\subseteq X$ is complete pluripolar if every point of $X$ has a neighborhood $U$ with a plurisubharmonic function $p$ on $U$ such that $A\cap U=\{ p=-\infty \} $. A quasi-plurisubharmonic function has small unbounded locus if it is locally bounded outside a closed complete pluripolar set. Definition 6.8.5 . 990C506B7D25 Let $\mathcal O_ X$ denote the sheaf of holomorphic functions on $X$. For a quasi-plurisubharmonic function $u$ on $X$, the multiplier ideal $\mathcal I(u)\subseteq \mathcal O_ X$ is the ideal sheaf whose sections over an open set $U$ are the holomorphic functions $g$ on $U$ for which $|g|^2\mathrm{e}^{-u}$ is locally integrable on $U$ with respect to a smooth positive volume form. Its stalk at $x$ is denoted by $\mathcal I(u)_ x$. Changing the volume form does not change local integrability: on relatively compact coordinate neighborhoods, the ratio of two smooth positive volume forms is bounded above and below by positive constants. In particular, the definition does not involve a choice of Hermitian metric, and it applies verbatim to quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on any complex manifold. Proposition 5.33.2 . 32843D040902 If $u\preceq v$, then $\mathcal I(ku)\subseteq \mathcal I(kv)$ for every real $k>0$. If $u\sim v$, then these ideals agree for every $k>0$. Proof. Let $g$ be a local holomorphic function on $X$. If $u\leq v+C$, then $\mathrm{e}^{-kv}\leq \mathrm{e}^{kC}\mathrm{e}^{-ku}$. Multiplying by $|g|^2$ shows that local integrability of $|g|^2\mathrm{e}^{-ku}$ implies local integrability of $|g|^2\mathrm{e}^{-kv}$. If $u\sim v$, the same argument applies in both directions. $\square$ Example 5.33.3 . 36A8480CE7DF On a disk in $\mathbb C$ centered at the origin, with coordinate $z$, let $\lambda \geq 0$ and put $u(z)=\lambda \log |z|^2$ for $\lambda >0$, while $u=0$ for $\lambda =0$. Then \[  \mathcal I(u)_0=(z^{\lfloor \lambda \rfloor }).  \] Indeed, if a nonzero holomorphic germ has order $m$ at the origin, its squared modulus is comparable to $|z|^{2m}$ near the origin. In polar coordinates, its weighted integral over a disk of sufficiently small radius $\epsilon >0$ is finite precisely when \[  \int _0^\epsilon r^{2m-2\lambda +1}\, \mathrm{d}r<\infty , \qquad \text{equivalently}\qquad m>\lambda -1.  \] The smallest nonnegative integer satisfying this strict inequality is $\lfloor \lambda \rfloor $. When $\lambda $ is an integer, the borderline exponent $-1$ occurs for $m=\lambda -1$ and gives a divergent integral; this is where the strictness of the inequality matters. The example also shows that a single multiplier ideal does not determine the singularity: different coefficients $\lambda $ can have the same integer part. For a real weight $k>0$, the same calculation applied to $ku$ gives $\mathcal I(ku)_0=(z^{\lfloor k\lambda \rfloor })$. The ideals at all weights $k>0$ recover $\lambda $: if $0\leq \lambda <\mu $, the integer parts of $k\lambda $ and $k\mu $ differ as soon as $k(\mu -\lambda )>1$. We therefore compare multiplier ideals at all positive weights. For quasi-plurisubharmonic functions $u,v$, we write $u\preceq _{\mathcal I}v$ if $\mathcal I(ku)\subseteq \mathcal I(kv)$ for every real $k>0$, and $u\sim _{\mathcal I}v$ if $\mathcal I(ku)=\mathcal I(kv)$ for every real $k>0$. We call $\preceq _{\mathcal I}$ the ideal order ; if $u\sim _{\mathcal I}v$, then $u$ and $v$ have the same multiplier-ideal type , or ideal type . By proposition 5.33.2 , $u\preceq v$ implies $u\preceq _{\mathcal I}v$, and $u\sim v$ implies $u\sim _{\mathcal I}v$. These relations make sense on any complex manifold. Their relation to envelopes and to global masses requires further arguments; see section 18.2 .

title: Proposition 5.33.1
text: Proposition 5.33.1 . EFC5ED339FC3 The relation $\preceq $ is a preorder, and $\sim $ is an equivalence relation. If $u$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic and $f$ is a smooth function on $X$, then $u+f\sim u$. In particular, all smooth functions on $X$ have the same singularity type. Proof. Reflexivity follows with $C=0$. If $u\leq v+C$ and $v\leq w+D$, then $u\leq w+C+D$, which proves transitivity. As for every preorder, comparison in both directions defines an equivalence relation. Since $X$ is compact, a smooth function $f$ satisfies $|f|\leq A$ for some constant $A$, and then $u-A\leq u+f\leq u+A$. Taking $u=0$ shows that every smooth function has the singularity type of the constants. $\square$

title: Proposition 5.33.2
text: Proposition 5.33.2 . 32843D040902 If $u\preceq v$, then $\mathcal I(ku)\subseteq \mathcal I(kv)$ for every real $k>0$. If $u\sim v$, then these ideals agree for every $k>0$. Proof. Let $g$ be a local holomorphic function on $X$. If $u\leq v+C$, then $\mathrm{e}^{-kv}\leq \mathrm{e}^{kC}\mathrm{e}^{-ku}$. Multiplying by $|g|^2$ shows that local integrability of $|g|^2\mathrm{e}^{-ku}$ implies local integrability of $|g|^2\mathrm{e}^{-kv}$. If $u\sim v$, the same argument applies in both directions. $\square$

title: Example 5.33.3
text: Example 5.33.3 . 36A8480CE7DF On a disk in $\mathbb C$ centered at the origin, with coordinate $z$, let $\lambda \geq 0$ and put $u(z)=\lambda \log |z|^2$ for $\lambda >0$, while $u=0$ for $\lambda =0$. Then \[  \mathcal I(u)_0=(z^{\lfloor \lambda \rfloor }).  \] Indeed, if a nonzero holomorphic germ has order $m$ at the origin, its squared modulus is comparable to $|z|^{2m}$ near the origin. In polar coordinates, its weighted integral over a disk of sufficiently small radius $\epsilon >0$ is finite precisely when \[  \int _0^\epsilon r^{2m-2\lambda +1}\, \mathrm{d}r<\infty , \qquad \text{equivalently}\qquad m>\lambda -1.  \] The smallest nonnegative integer satisfying this strict inequality is $\lfloor \lambda \rfloor $. When $\lambda $ is an integer, the borderline exponent $-1$ occurs for $m=\lambda -1$ and gives a divergent integral; this is where the strictness of the inequality matters.

title: 5.34 Analytic types and restriction
text:
The simplest singularities of quasi-plurisubharmonic functions are logarithmic poles along the common zeros of finitely many holomorphic functions. The logarithmic growth of a general singularity at a point is measured by its Lelong number. Let $u$ be a quasi-plurisubharmonic function on a complex manifold and let $x$ be a point. Choose holomorphic coordinates centered at $x$ and a smooth function $q$ such that $p=u+q$ is plurisubharmonic near $x$, and write $B(x,r)$ for the Euclidean coordinate ball of radius $r$. The Lelong number of $u$ at $x$ is \[  
u (u,x)=\lim _{r\downarrow 0}  rac{\sup _{B(x,r)}p}{\log r^2}.  \] By the local growth theorem recalled in Proposition 6.7.1 , the limit exists and does not depend on the coordinates or on the correction $q$. With this normalization, $\log |z|^2$ has Lelong number one at the origin. For an irreducible analytic subset $Z$, the generic Lelong number of $u$ along $Z$ is \[  
u (u,Z)=\inf _{x\in Z}
u (u,x).  \] By Siu's theorem, recalled in 5.34.2 , $
u (u,x)=
u (u,Z)$ for all $x\in Z$ outside a countable union of proper analytic subsets of $Z$. For analytic singularities we use the convention of Definition 6.14.5 : we say that a quasi-plurisubharmonic function $u$ has analytic singularities if near every point there are holomorphic functions $f_1,\ldots ,f_ N$, not all identically zero, and a rational number $c>0$ such that \[  u=c\log  igl (|f_1|^2+\cdots +|f_ N|^2 igr )+O(1), \qquad c\in \mathbb Q_{>0}.  \] The remainder is only required to be bounded; if it can be chosen smooth, we say that $u$ has analytic singularities with smooth remainder . Given a coherent ideal sheaf $\mathfrak a$ and a common coefficient $c$, we say that $u$ has analytic type $(c,\mathfrak a)$ if this holds with local generators $f_1,\ldots ,f_ N$ of $\mathfrak a$. The choice of generators does not matter: two finite systems of generators of the same ideal change the logarithm only by a bounded amount on smaller relatively compact open sets. Proposition 5.34.1 . AAD8908A0CF9 Analytic singularities are preserved by addition, finite maxima, and multiplication by positive rational numbers. Let $u$ have analytic type $(c,\mathfrak a)$, and let $Y\subset X$ be a connected complex submanifold on which $\mathfrak a$ does not vanish identically. Then the restriction $u|_ Y$ is a quasi-plurisubharmonic function on $Y$, in particular not identically $-\infty $, and it has analytic type \[  (c,\mathfrak a\mathcal O_ Y).  \] Here $\mathfrak a\mathcal O_ Y$ is the image ideal, generated by the restrictions to $Y$ of local sections of $\mathfrak a$. Proof. For multiplication by a positive rational number, multiply the coefficient. Consider two presentations with coefficients $c_1,c_2$ and ideals $\mathfrak a_1,\mathfrak a_2$, and choose a positive rational number $d$ with $c_1=k d$ and $c_2=\ell d$, where $k,\ell $ are positive integers. Raising a sum of squared moduli of generators of $\mathfrak a_1$ to the power $k$ gives, up to bounded factors, the corresponding sum for $\mathfrak a_1^ k$; similarly for $\mathfrak a_2^\ell $. Products of generators of $\mathfrak a_1^ k$ and $\mathfrak a_2^\ell $ therefore present the sum with coefficient $d$, since a product of sums of squares is a sum of squares of pairwise products. For the maximum, apply the elementary inequalities \[  \max \{ A,B\} \leq A+B\leq 2\max \{ A,B\} ,\qquad A,B\geq 0,  \] to the two sums of squared moduli of generators of $\mathfrak a_1^ k$ and $\mathfrak a_2^\ell $. Taking logarithms shows that the maximum differs from $d$ times the logarithm of their total by a bounded amount. These are local assertions; on the compact manifold, finitely many charts give the corresponding comparisons of ordinary singularity types. For the restriction, restrict to $Y$ the two-sided bounds that define the remainder. Since $Y$ is connected and is not contained in the zero set of $\mathfrak a$, the common zero set of the restricted generators is a proper analytic subset of $Y$, so $u|_ Y$ is finite on a dense open subset of $Y$. After a smooth local correction, the restriction theorem for plurisubharmonic functions shows that $u|_ Y$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic, and the restricted bounds give the asserted presentation. $\square$ For an arbitrary quasi-plurisubharmonic function, a vanishing generic Lelong number along a submanifold does not prevent the restriction from being identically $-\infty $. For example, on a small polydisk in $\mathbb C^ n$ with coordinates $z=(z_1,\ldots ,z_ n)$ and $|z_1|<\mathrm{e}^{-1}$, the function \[  u(z)=-\sqrt{-\log |z_1|^2}  \] is plurisubharmonic, because $t\mapsto -\sqrt{-t}$ is increasing and convex for $t<0$. Its Lelong number vanishes at every point of $\{ z_1=0\} $, but its restriction to this hyperplane is identically $-\infty $. For the analytic approximants constructed below, the analytic hypothesis in proposition 5.34.1 excludes this behavior.

title: 5.34.2 Lelong level sets
text:
Siu's analyticity theorem states that, for every quasi-plurisubharmonic function $u$ and every $c>0$, the upper level set $\{ x:
u (u,x)\geq c\} $ is an analytic subset. After a smooth local correction, this is the theorem for closed positive currents, which we use in the form recalled in Theorem 6.9.5 (Siu) ; see section 25.3 for the original source. For a closed positive current, the Lelong monotonicity formula also bounds the trace mass of small balls. The resulting Hausdorff estimate shows that a closed positive $(j,j)$-current puts no mass on sets of zero Hausdorff $2(n-j)$-measure. Corollary 5.34.3 . C6F4FBF73B9E Let $T$ be a closed positive $(j,j)$-current on a complex manifold of dimension $n$, with $1\leq j<n$. Its coefficient measures vanish on every Borel set of zero Hausdorff $2(n-j)$-measure. Proof. In a coordinate chart put $\kappa =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}|z|^2$ and $\mu =T\wedge \kappa ^{n-j}$. By the Lelong monotonicity formula in bidimension $(n-j,n-j)$, the function $r\mapsto r^{-2(n-j)}\mu (B(x,r))$ is nondecreasing; see [ Chapter III, formulas (5.5)–(5.8), pp. 158–159 , DemCADG ] . Fix a relatively compact inner chart and a radius $r_0>0$ such that all balls of radius $r_0$ centered in it lie in a fixed compact subset of the chart. Their masses are bounded by the mass of that compact set. Hence \[  \mu (B(x,r))\leq Cr^{2(n-j)},\qquad 0<r\leq r_0,  \] uniformly for centers in the inner chart. A Borel set in the inner chart with zero Hausdorff $2(n-j)$-measure can be covered by balls $B(x_ i,r_ i)$ with $\sum _ ir_ i^{2(n-j)}$ arbitrarily small, so it has zero $\mu $-mass. Since $T$ is positive, the total variation of each of its coefficient measures is bounded by a constant multiple of $\mu $. A countable cover by charts proves the assertion. $\square$ The non-strict inequality in Siu's theorem cannot be replaced by a strict one, even on a compact Kähler manifold. Example 5.34.4 . 697E97CED780 Let $X=\mathbb P^2$, with homogeneous coordinates $[x:y:z]$, and let $\sigma $ be the Fubini–Study form normalized by $\int _ X\sigma ^2=1$. Put $\| Z\| ^2=|x|^2+|y|^2+|z|^2$, $a_ j=2^{-j}$ and $\lambda _ j=2^{-j-1}$ for $j\geq 1$. The global function \[  u([Z])=\log  rac{|y|^2}{\| Z\| ^2} +\sum _{j\geq 1}\lambda _ j \log  rac{|x-a_ jz|^2}{(1+a_ j^2)\| Z\| ^2}  \] belongs to $\mathrm{PSH}(X, rac32\sigma )$. For the line $D=\{ y=0\} $ and the points $p_ j=[a_ j:0:1]$, it satisfies \[  \{ 
u (u,\cdot )\geq 1\} =D, \qquad \{ 
u (u,\cdot )>1\} =\{ p_ j:j\geq 1\} .  \] The second set is not analytic. Proof. For a linear form $\ell $ with coefficient vector of norm one, the function $v_\ell =\log (|\ell (Z)|^2/\| Z\| ^2)$ is nonpositive and satisfies $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_\ell =[\ell =0]-\sigma $. Its $L^1(X,\sigma ^2)$ norm is finite and independent of $\ell $, because the unitary group $U(3)$ acts on homogeneous coordinates, preserves $\sigma $, and acts transitively on such forms. Since $\sum _ j\lambda _ j=1/2$, the partial sums of the series defining $u$ decrease to an $L^1$ function. They have the common curvature lower bound $- rac32\sigma $, so their limit is quasi-plurisubharmonic and \[  T:=	frac 32\sigma +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u=[D]+\sum _{j\geq 1}\lambda _ j[L_ j], \qquad L_ j=\{ x-a_ jz=0\} .  \] The series of positive closed currents converges, since every line has $\sigma $-trace mass one and the coefficients are summable. We compute the Lelong numbers from the local mass formula. In affine coordinates $w=(w_1,w_2)$ centered at a point $q$, put $\kappa =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}|w|^2$. An affine complex line $H$ at distance $d$ from $q$ satisfies \[  \int _{H\cap B(q,r)}\kappa =(r^2-d^2)_+.  \] Consequently $r^{-2}\int _{H\cap B(q,r)}\kappa $ is at most one and tends to $\mathbf1_ H(q)$ as $r\downarrow 0$; a line that does not meet the chart contributes zero. Tonelli's theorem and dominated convergence for the summable coefficients therefore give \[  
u (u,q)=
u (T,q) =\mathbf1_ D(q)+\sum _{j\geq 1}\lambda _ j\mathbf1_{L_ j}(q).  \] Here we used that a smooth local correction does not change the Lelong number. The computation also covers points at which infinitely many lines accumulate. The lines $L_ j$ meet $D$ at the distinct points $p_ j$ and meet one another only at $p_\infty =[0:1:0]
otin D$. Thus $
u (u,p_ j)=1+\lambda _ j$, whereas $
u (u,q)=1$ for $q\in D\setminus \{ p_ j:j\geq 1\} $. Outside $D$, the Lelong number is at most $\sum _ j\lambda _ j=1/2$. This proves the two level-set identities. Finally, $p_ j	o p_*=[0:0:1]$ and $
u (u,p_*)=1$, so the strict level set is not closed and hence not analytic. $\square$

title: 5.35 The local Bergman estimates
text:
Demailly's approximation of plurisubharmonic functions by functions with analytic singularities is built from Bergman kernels of weighted spaces of holomorphic functions. In this section we recall the local construction and its estimates. Fix a bounded pseudoconvex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$ and a plurisubharmonic function $\psi $ on $\Omega $. Write $\mathrm{d}\lambda $ for Euclidean volume and $B(x,r)$ for the Euclidean ball of radius $r>0$ about $x$. For a positive integer $m$, define the weighted Hilbert space of holomorphic functions \[  \mathcal H_ m=\left\{ f\in \mathcal O(\Omega ): \| f\| _ m^2:=\int _\Omega |f|^2\mathrm{e}^{-m\psi }\, \mathrm{d}\lambda <\infty ight\} .  \] Choose an orthonormal basis $(g_{m,j})_ j$ of $\mathcal H_ m$ and define $ eta _ m=m^{-1}\log \sum _ j|g_{m,j}|^2$. The sum is the squared norm of point evaluation, \[  \sum _ j|g_{m,j}(x)|^2 =\sup _{\| f\| _ m\leq 1}|f(x)|^2,  \] and is therefore independent of the basis. By the local finite generation part of Bergman regularization, $ eta _ m$ has analytic type $(1/m,\mathcal I(m\psi ))$ on relatively compact open subsets of $\Omega $. This follows from the generation of the multiplier ideal by weighted $L^2$ holomorphic functions and from local $L^2$ division; see [ Proposition 5.7 and Section 14.A , DemAM11 ] . We use this local statement, together with the point-extension estimate in the proof below, as a standard input. Proposition 5.35.1 . DBEB8E0E0318 There are constants $C_1,C_2$ independent of $m$ such that, for $B(x,r)\Subset \Omega $, BFDE2F85F930 5.35.2  egin{equation}  \psi (x)- rac{C_1}{m} \leq  eta _ m(x) \leq \sup _{B(x,r)}\psi + rac1m\log  rac{C_2}{r^{2n}}. \end{equation} Consequently $ eta _ m	o \psi $ pointwise and in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$, and F9AE1A865ACD 5.35.3  egin{equation}  \max \{ 
u (\psi ,x)-n/m,0\}  \leq 
u ( eta _ m,x)\leq 
u (\psi ,x). \end{equation} Proof. For $\| f\| _ m\leq 1$, the submean inequality gives \[  |f(x)|^2 \leq C_2r^{-2n}\int _{B(x,r)}|f|^2\, \mathrm{d}\lambda \leq C_2r^{-2n}\mathrm{e}^{m\sup _{B(x,r)}\psi }.  \] Taking the supremum over the unit ball of $\mathcal H_ m$ and then the logarithm proves the upper bound. For the lower bound, suppose that $\psi (x)>-\infty $. The local Ohsawa–Takegoshi point-extension theorem gives a holomorphic $f$ with $f(x)=1$ and \[  \int _\Omega |f|^2\mathrm{e}^{-m\psi }\, \mathrm{d}\lambda \leq C \mathrm{e}^{-m\psi (x)},  \] where the constant is independent of the plurisubharmonic weight and of $m$. After normalizing $f$ in $\mathcal H_ m$, we see that the squared norm of point evaluation is at least $C^{-1}\mathrm{e}^{m\psi (x)}$, which proves the lower bound. At a pole of $\psi $ the lower bound holds trivially. Choosing $r=1/m$ in the upper bound and using upper semicontinuity of $\psi $ proves pointwise convergence. On a fixed relatively compact set, the same estimates bound $ eta _ m$ above by a constant and below by $\psi -C_1/m$. Since $\psi $ is locally integrable, dominated convergence also gives convergence in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$. For the Lelong estimate, take suprema over $B(x,r)$ in the two inequalities, bounding the right-hand side of the upper one by a supremum over $B(x,2r)$. Divide by $\log r^2<0$ and let $r\downarrow 0$. After the division, the term $-(2n/m)\log r$ contributes $-n/m$, while the constant terms disappear. This proves the two inequalities in ( 5.35.3 ); since Lelong numbers are nonnegative, the lower bound may be replaced by its maximum with zero. $\square$ In [ DemAM11 ] , the local weight is $\mathrm{e}^{-2m\phi }$ and Lelong numbers are normalized by $\log |z|$. With $\psi =2\phi $, these conventions give exactly the formulas above; in particular, the loss is $n/m$ for the weight $\mathrm{e}^{-m\psi }$ and the normalization by $\log |z|^2$. The same construction and estimates hold for every real $m>0$. The coefficient $1/m$ of the resulting logarithmic presentation is rational exactly when $m$ is rational, and we speak of an analytic type only in that case. The global sequence constructed below is indexed by integers. For a quasi-plurisubharmonic function $u$, the generators of $\mathcal I(mu)$ also control the multiplier ideals of $u$ at nearby weights; a small loss in the weight compensates for the finite Bergman index. Lemma 5.35.4 . FE03F7C266DD Let $u$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic, let $m>0$, and let $a_ m$ be a function which locally satisfies $a_ m=m^{-1}\log \sum _ k|g_ k|^2+O(1)$, where the $g_ k$ generate $\mathcal I(mu)$. For $t>0$ and $s>1$, \[  \mathcal I(sta_ m)\subseteq \mathcal I(tu) \qquad 	ext{whenever}\qquad m\geq  rac{st}{s-1}.  \] Moreover, $u\preceq a_ m$ locally, and hence $\mathcal I(tu)\subseteq \mathcal I(ta_ m)$ for every $t>0$. Proof. On a sufficiently small coordinate neighborhood, choose generators $g_1,\ldots ,g_ N$ of $\mathcal I(mu)$ and put $B=(\sum _ k|g_ k|^2)\mathrm{e}^{-mu}$. After shrinking the neighborhood, $B$ is integrable and $a_ m=m^{-1}\log \sum _ k|g_ k|^2+O(1)$ with a bounded remainder. If $f\in \mathcal I(sta_ m)$, shrink once more so that $f$ is bounded and $A=|f|^2\mathrm{e}^{-sta_ m}$ is integrable. Then, almost everywhere, \[  |f|^2\mathrm{e}^{-tu} \leq C|f|^{2-2/s}A^{1/s}B^{t/m}.  \] Hölder's inequality with exponents $s$ and $s/(s-1)$ applies because $st/(m(s-1))\leq 1$, and it shows that the left side is locally integrable, also in the case of equality in the bound for $m$. Finally, the local Bergman lower estimate of proposition 5.35.1 gives $u\preceq a_ m$ locally; bounded smooth corrections affect neither this comparison nor any of the ideals. $\square$

Lemma 5.35.4
text: Lemma 5.35.4 . FE03F7C266DD Let $u$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic, let $m>0$, and let $a_ m$ be a function which locally satisfies $a_ m=m^{-1}\log \sum _ k|g_ k|^2+O(1)$, where the $g_ k$ generate $\mathcal I(mu)$. For $t>0$ and $s>1$, \[  \mathcal I(sta_ m)\subseteq \mathcal I(tu) \qquad \text{whenever}\qquad m\geq \frac{st}{s-1}.  \] Moreover, $u\preceq a_ m$ locally, and hence $\mathcal I(tu)\subseteq \mathcal I(ta_ m)$ for every $t>0$. Proof. On a sufficiently small coordinate neighborhood, choose generators $g_1,\ldots ,g_ N$ of $\mathcal I(mu)$ and put $B=(\sum _ k|g_ k|^2)\mathrm{e}^{-mu}$. After shrinking the neighborhood, $B$ is integrable and $a_ m=m^{-1}\log \sum _ k|g_ k|^2+O(1)$ with a bounded remainder. If $f\in \mathcal I(sta_ m)$, shrink once more so that $f$ is bounded and $A=|f|^2\mathrm{e}^{-sta_ m}$ is integrable. Then, almost everywhere, \[  |f|^2\mathrm{e}^{-tu} \leq C|f|^{2-2/s}A^{1/s}B^{t/m}.  \] Hölder's inequality with exponents $s$ and $s/(s-1)$ applies because $st/(m(s-1))\leq 1$, and it shows that the left side is locally integrable, also in the case of equality in the bound for $m$. Finally, the local Bergman lower estimate of proposition 5.35.1 gives $u\preceq a_ m$ locally; bounded smooth corrections affect neither this comparison nor any of the ideals. $\square$

title: 5.36 The global curvature bound
text:
We return to the compact manifold $X$ with its Hermitian form $\omega $. Demailly's global regularization theorem glues the local Bergman constructions while controlling the curvature error. We use it as a classical input in the following form. Theorem 5.36.1 (Demailly regularization) . 3CA98F11CC5B Let $u$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic on $X$ and let $\gamma $ be a continuous real $(1,1)$-form with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\geq \gamma $. There are quasi-plurisubharmonic functions $u_ m$, defined for all sufficiently large positive integers $m$, and numbers $\epsilon _ m\downarrow 0$ such that $u_ m$ has analytic type $(1/m,\mathcal I(mu))$; $u_ m\geq u$ and $u_ m	o u$ pointwise and in $L^1(X)$; $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ m\geq \gamma -\epsilon _ m\omega $; $\max \{ 
u (u,x)-n/m,0\} \leq 
u (u_ m,x)\leq 
u (u,x)$ for all $x$. The sequence $(u_ m)$ need not be monotone. This is the form of [ Theorem 14.12 , DemAM11 ] used here. The local generators in the construction are the weighted Bergman generators of $\mathcal I(mu)$; smooth local corrections do not change this ideal. On overlaps the local Bergman sums are comparable, so the glued logarithm keeps the analytic type $(1/m,\mathcal I(mu))$. The construction freezes the continuous lower bound $\gamma $ on sufficiently small coordinate balls, and its curvature error combines the modulus of continuity of $\gamma $ with an overlap term that tends to zero as $m$ increases. It is this global curvature estimate, and not merely the local convergence of proposition 5.35.1 , that we take from the theorem. Corollary 5.36.2 . 8F2184BBF4C4 Let $	heta $ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ and $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. The approximants $u_ m$ of theorem 5.36.1 for $\gamma =-	heta $ satisfy \[  	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ m\geq -\epsilon _ m\omega .  \] In particular, they have analytic type $(1/m,\mathcal I(mu))$. Proof. Apply theorem 5.36.1 to $u$ with the lower bound $\gamma =-	heta $; the theorem does not require $\gamma $ to be closed. Adding $	heta $ to the curvature inequality gives the assertion. In the normalization of [ DemAM11 ] , the theorem is applied to the potential $u/2$, since $ rac{\mathrm{i}}{\pi }\partial  ar\partial (u/2)=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$. $\square$ Thus the approximants keep the curvature lower bound up to an error that tends to zero. Their multiplier ideals determine the limit of their ordinary envelopes; see theorem 18.7.6 .

title: Corollary 5.36.2

title: 5.36.3 Regularization of closed currents
text:
We also use the regularization of closed currents in the form recalled in 5.18 Analytic singularities . Let $T=\eta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v$ be a closed real $(1,1)$-current, where $\eta $ is a smooth closed form and $v$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic, and set $
u (T,x)=
u (v,x)$. Suppose that $T\geq \gamma $ for a smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\gamma $. Smooth regularization gives smooth representatives $T_ j=\eta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j$ with \[  T_ j\geq \gamma -C\lambda _ j\omega ,  \] where $C>0$ is a fixed constant and the continuous functions $\lambda _ j$ decrease pointwise to $
u (T,\cdot )$. If all Lelong numbers of $T$ vanish, Dini's theorem shows that $\lambda _ j	o 0$ uniformly, so the loss of positivity becomes uniformly small. Analytic regularization instead gives representatives $S_ j$ with analytic singularities and \[  S_ j\geq \gamma -\varepsilon _ j\omega ,\qquad \varepsilon _ j\downarrow 0,\qquad 
u (S_ j,x)\leq 
u (T,x).  \] Thus analytic regularization preserves strict positivity up to a small loss and creates no positive Lelong number at a point where the Lelong number of $T$ vanishes.

title: 5.36.4 Smooth remainders after resolution
text: For arguments on a modification, the bounded remainder in an analytic presentation is sometimes insufficient. The following version of regularization gives a smooth remainder after resolution. Theorem 5.36.5 (Demailly regularization) . 88038BD901A0 Let $\alpha $ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form and let $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\alpha )$. There are numbers $\delta _ j\downarrow 0$ and functions $\widetilde u_ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\alpha +\delta _ j\omega )$ decreasing to $u$ with the following properties. Each $\widetilde u_ j$ is smooth outside an analytic pole set, and there is a modification $\pi _ j:Y_ j\to X$, obtained by a finite sequence of blowups with smooth centers, such that locally on $Y_ j$ \[  \pi _ j^*\widetilde u_ j=\sum _\ell a_\ell \log |s_\ell |^2+b, \qquad a_\ell >0,\quad b\in C^\infty .  \] Here the $s_\ell $ are local holomorphic defining functions of divisors, the $a_\ell >0$ are real numbers, and $b$ is a smooth real function. The divisors may be taken to have simple normal crossings. This classical theorem is applied to the closed current $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ with the smooth lower bound $-\alpha $; see section 25.3 for its source. The lower bound need not be closed, and $X$ need not be Kähler. What matters here is the smooth remainder $b$ after resolution; an analytic type, whose remainder is merely bounded, would not suffice. The sequence $(\widetilde u_ j)$ need not be the multiplier-ideal sequence of theorem 5.36.1 , and we do not claim that the conclusions of the two theorems hold for one and the same sequence. If $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\geq \varepsilon \omega $ for some $\varepsilon >0$, applying the theorem with $\alpha =\theta -\varepsilon \omega $ and discarding the terms with $\delta _ j\geq \varepsilon $ gives approximants with $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\widetilde u_ j\geq (\varepsilon -\delta _ j)\omega >0$; thus strict positivity is preserved.

title: 5.37 Multiplier ideals and logarithmic poles
text:
For a logarithmic pole along a submanifold, weighted integrability of a holomorphic germ is determined by its vanishing order in the normal directions. For general singularities, the valuative characterization of multiplier ideals and the strong openness theorem, both recalled in Theorem 5.16.21 (Guan–Zhou) , make the comparison of multiplier ideals compatible with maxima, sums and increasing limits. In local coordinates $(z,w)\in \mathbb C^ d	imes \mathbb C^ k$, with $d\geq 0$ and $k\geq 1$, let $Y=\{ w=0\} $ and denote its ideal by $\mathcal I_ Y$. Lemma 5.37.1 . C21A2A6F9E07 If a quasi-plurisubharmonic function has the form $u=c\log |w|^2+O(1)$ with $c>0$ and locally bounded remainder, then for every $t>0$, \[  \mathcal I(tu)=\mathcal I_ Y^{\max \{ \lfloor tcfloor -k+1,0\} }.  \] The zeroth power is the full structure sheaf. Proof. The bounded remainder changes the weight only by bounded positive factors. Expand a nonzero holomorphic germ $g(z,w)$ in homogeneous polynomials in $w$, and let $a$ be the smallest degree whose term does not vanish identically. On smaller product neighborhoods, $|g(z,w)|\leq C|w|^ a$. Hence $a+k>tc$ suffices for weighted integrability, since the corresponding radial integral in $ho =|w|$ is \[  \int _0^\varepsilon ho ^{2a-2tc+2k-1}\, \mathrm{d}ho <+\infty .  \] Conversely, let $z$ be a point near the origin at which the term of degree $a$ does not vanish identically in $w$. Integration of $|g(z,w)|^2$ over the spheres $|w|=ho $ gives a positive leading term of order $ho ^{2a}$, so the radial integral in $w$ diverges when $a+k\leq tc$, logarithmically in the case of equality. Such points $z$ form a nonempty open set in every sufficiently small neighborhood, and Fubini's theorem shows that $g$ is not weighted-integrable near the origin. For $d=0$ this is the radial calculation at a point. Thus $g$ is weighted-integrable exactly when $a\geq \lfloor tcfloor -k+1$, that is, when $g$ lies in the power of $\mathcal I_ Y$ given in the statement. $\square$ Cutoff functions allow us to insert small isolated logarithmic poles into any Hermitian background. Lemma 5.37.2 . EBB1890494B1 Let $\omega $ be a Hermitian form on $X$, and fix distinct points $p_1,\ldots ,p_ N$ of $X$. There are constants $C_ j>0$ such that, whenever $a_ j>0$ and $\sum _ jC_ ja_ j<1$, there is $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$, smooth off these points, with \[  u=a_ j\log |z|^2+O(1)\quad \hbox{near }p_ j,\qquad \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\geq \left(1-\sum _ jC_ ja_ jight)\omega .  \] Here $z$ denotes local coordinates centered at $p_ j$. The function can be chosen to vanish outside arbitrarily small disjoint coordinate neighborhoods, with the constants depending on those neighborhoods. Proof. Choose disjoint coordinate balls centered at the points $p_ j$ and smooth cutoffs $\chi _ j$ supported in them and equal to one near their centers. The function $\chi _ j\log |z|^2$, extended by zero, is plurisubharmonic near its pole and smooth elsewhere, so its complex Hessian is bounded below by $-C_ j\omega $. Set $u=\sum _ ja_ j\chi _ j\log |z|^2$. These lower bounds give the asserted current inequality, and the remaining properties follow from the disjointness of the supports. $\square$ Theorem 5.37.3 . 3F1FC2F620B4 Let $u,v$ be plurisubharmonic functions near a point of $\mathbb C^ n$. By a local modification we mean a modification $\pi $, with smooth source, of a neighborhood of this point. The inclusions $\mathcal I(ku)\subseteq \mathcal I(kv)$ for every real $k>0$ are equivalent to the inequalities $
u (u\circ \pi ,y)\geq 
u (v\circ \pi ,y)$ at every point $y$ of the source of every local modification $\pi $. Likewise, equality of the multiplier ideals at every positive weight is equivalent to equality of all these Lelong numbers. If $p_ j$ is an increasing sequence of plurisubharmonic functions converging almost everywhere to a plurisubharmonic function $p$, then, for each point $x$ and each $\lambda >0$, \[  \mathcal I(\lambda p_ j)_ x=\mathcal I(\lambda p)_ x \quad 	ext{for all sufficiently large }j.  \] In the first item, the neighborhoods may be shrunk as necessary; we never need to extend a local modification to a modification of a compact manifold. The second item is the increasing-limit form of the strong openness theorem used in Theorem 5.16.21 (Guan–Zhou) . Since adding a smooth function changes neither multiplier ideals nor Lelong numbers, both items apply to quasi-plurisubharmonic functions after the local correction of proposition 5.22.2 . Lemma 5.37.4 . ACC2529A680B Let $u,u',v,v'$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$. For any quasi-plurisubharmonic $h$, one has \[  u+h\sim _{\mathcal I}v+h \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad u\sim _{\mathcal I}v.  \] If $u\sim _{\mathcal I}v$ and $u'\sim _{\mathcal I}v'$, then \[  \max (u,u')\sim _{\mathcal I}\max (v,v'),\qquad u+u'\sim _{\mathcal I}v+v',\qquad a u\sim _{\mathcal I}a v\quad (a>0).  \] Proof. Fix a coordinate neighborhood $U\subset X$ and a modification $\pi :Y	o U$ with smooth source. At every $y\in Y$, the elementary rules for the Lelong numbers of maxima, sums and positive multiples give \[   egin{aligned}  
u (\max (u,u')\circ \pi ,y) & =\min \{ 
u (u\circ \pi ,y),
u (u'\circ \pi ,y)\} ,\  
u ((u+u')\circ \pi ,y) & =
u (u\circ \pi ,y)+
u (u'\circ \pi ,y),\  
u (a u\circ \pi ,y)& =a
u (u\circ \pi ,y). \end{aligned}  \] These rules are unaffected by smooth local corrections. Since $u\sim _{\mathcal I}v$ and $u'\sim _{\mathcal I}v'$, the first item of theorem 5.37.3 shows that the right-hand sides do not change when $u,u'$ are replaced by $v,v'$. The converse direction of the same item, applied on each coordinate neighborhood, gives the three asserted equivalences. For the cancellation rule, suppose that $u+h\sim _{\mathcal I}v+h$. By the first item of theorem 5.37.3 , the pullbacks $(u+h)\circ \pi $ and $(v+h)\circ \pi $ have the same Lelong numbers. The common summand $h\circ \pi $ is quasi-plurisubharmonic, so its Lelong numbers are finite, and subtracting them shows that $u\circ \pi $ and $v\circ \pi $ have the same Lelong numbers. Hence $u\sim _{\mathcal I}v$ by the same item. The reverse implication is the addition rule proved above. $\square$ A residual with zero Lelong numbers can still be unbounded, but it does not change any multiplier ideal, even after addition to another potential. Lemma 5.37.5 . 5929CFA4B87F Let $q$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic on a complex manifold and suppose that $
u (q,x)=0$ at every point. Then $\mathrm e^{-tq}$ is locally integrable for every $t>0$. For every quasi-plurisubharmonic $v$ and every $t>0$, \[  \mathcal I igl (t(v+q) igr )=\mathcal I(tv).  \] Proof. Fix a point $x$ and add a smooth correction to make $q$ plurisubharmonic on a bounded pseudoconvex coordinate neighborhood. Form the weighted Bergman space of proposition 5.35.1 at weight $t$. If every member vanished at $x$, the Cauchy estimates, together with the local upper bound for $q$, would give \[  \sup _{\| g\| _ t\leq 1}|g(z)|\leq C|z-x|  \] near $x$. Its Bergman potential would consequently have Lelong number at least $1/t$, contradicting ( 5.35.3 ). There is therefore a weighted square-integrable holomorphic function nonzero at $x$. On a smaller neighborhood it is bounded away from zero, so its weighted norm proves integrability of $\mathrm e^{-tq}$. Smooth corrections do not change this conclusion. Thus $q\sim _{\mathcal I}0$; the addition rule in lemma 5.37.4 gives $v+q\sim _{\mathcal I}v$, which is precisely the asserted equality at every weight. $\square$ Let $v,w$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on an open set, and let $Y$ be a complex submanifold on which $v|_ Y$ is not identically $-\infty $. The restriction and subadditivity theorems give the two inclusions recalled in 6.10 Restriction, products and integral closure and : 582A3343A949 5.37.6  egin{equation}  \mathcal I(v|_ Y)\subseteq \mathcal I(v)\mathcal O_ Y, \qquad \mathcal I(v+w)\subseteq \mathcal I(v)\mathcal I(w). \end{equation} The first follows from the local Ohsawa–Takegoshi extension theorem. For the second, the weighted Hilbert space of holomorphic functions on a product is the Hilbert tensor product of the two weighted spaces, so the multiplier ideal of $v(x)+w(y)$ on the product is generated by products of generators of $\mathcal I(v)$ and $\mathcal I(w)$; the first inclusion, applied to the diagonal, then gives the second. These local results for plurisubharmonic functions extend to quasi-plurisubharmonic functions, in the weight convention of these constructions, by smooth corrections. Multiplier ideals commute with pullback by holomorphic submersions. Here the extension $\mathcal I\mathcal O_ Z$ of an ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ on $Y$ is the ideal sheaf on $Z$ generated by the pullbacks of its local sections. Lemma 5.37.7 . 2FA053FE56D9 Let $p:Z	o Y$ be a holomorphic submersion of complex manifolds and let $u\in \mathrm{QPSH}(Y)$. For every $t>0$, \[  \mathcal I(tu\circ p) =\mathcal I(tu)\mathcal O_ Z.  \] Proof. Work in product coordinates $(z,\zeta )$ with $p(z,\zeta )=z$. Write $\alpha $ for a multi-index in the fiber variables and $\mathrm{d}\lambda _\zeta $ for their Euclidean volume. A germ in the ideal on the right is a finite sum of bounded holomorphic multiples of pullbacks of germs that are square integrable against $\mathrm{e}^{-tu(z)}$. Fubini's theorem shows that it is weighted-integrable on a sufficiently small product neighborhood. Conversely, let $F(z,\zeta )$ be a weighted-integrable holomorphic germ and expand it in the fiber variables, \[  F(z,\zeta )=\sum _\alpha f_\alpha (z)\zeta ^\alpha .  \] The coefficient estimate for a holomorphic function on a polydisk gives, on smaller product neighborhoods, \[  |f_\alpha (z)|^2\leq C_\alpha \int |F(z,\zeta )|^2\, \mathrm{d}\lambda _\zeta .  \] Multiplying by $\mathrm{e}^{-tu(z)}$ and integrating in $z$ shows that each coefficient germ $f_\alpha $ belongs to $\mathcal I(tu)$. Let $J$ be the extension of this ideal to the local ring $R$ of holomorphic germs on the product. Every finite Taylor sum of $F$ belongs to $J$, and the remainder of total fiber degree at least $N$ belongs to $(\zeta )^ N$. Thus the class of $F$ in $R/J$ lies in $(\zeta )^ N(R/J)$ for every $N$. By the Krull intersection theorem for the finitely generated module $R/J$ over the Noetherian local ring $R$, the intersection of these submodules is zero. Hence $F\in J$. Smooth corrections and smooth positive volume densities do not change the integrability conditions. $\square$ Example 5.37.8 . E39EAA145A67 Exact multiplier-ideal pullback can fail at a critical fiber. On a polydisk in $\mathbb C^ n$, $n\geq 1$, let $f(z_0,\ldots ,z_{n-1})=z_0^2$ and put $v(t)=	frac 12\log |t|^2$. At the origin, \[  \mathcal I(v)=\mathcal O,\qquad \mathcal I(v\circ f)=(z_0) 
e \mathcal I(v)\mathcal O.  \] Proof. On the curve the coefficient is $1/2$, so the multiplier ideal is the zeroth power of the maximal ideal. Upstairs $v\circ f=\log |z_0|^2$ has coefficient one along the smooth divisor $\{ z_0=0\} $. Apply lemma 5.37.1 in codimension one to get its first ideal power. $\square$ This calculation concerns a fixed weight. For a surjective holomorphic map from a connected compact manifold to a curve, with connected fibers, pullback still preserves and reflects all-weight ideal types by 5.43.9 .

title: Theorem 5.37.3
text: Theorem 5.37.3 . 3F1FC2F620B4 Let $u,v$ be plurisubharmonic functions near a point of $\mathbb C^ n$. By a local modification we mean a modification $\pi $, with smooth source, of a neighborhood of this point. The inclusions $\mathcal I(ku)\subseteq \mathcal I(kv)$ for every real $k>0$ are equivalent to the inequalities $\nu (u\circ \pi ,y)\geq \nu (v\circ \pi ,y)$ at every point $y$ of the source of every local modification $\pi $. Likewise, equality of the multiplier ideals at every positive weight is equivalent to equality of all these Lelong numbers. If $p_ j$ is an increasing sequence of plurisubharmonic functions converging almost everywhere to a plurisubharmonic function $p$, then, for each point $x$ and each $\lambda >0$, \[  \mathcal I(\lambda p_ j)_ x=\mathcal I(\lambda p)_ x \quad \text{for all sufficiently large }j.  \]

title: Lemma 5.37.4
text:
Lemma 5.37.4 . ACC2529A680B Let $u,u',v,v'$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$. For any quasi-plurisubharmonic $h$, one has \[  u+h\sim _{\mathcal I}v+h \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad u\sim _{\mathcal I}v.  \] If $u\sim _{\mathcal I}v$ and $u'\sim _{\mathcal I}v'$, then \[  \max (u,u')\sim _{\mathcal I}\max (v,v'),\qquad u+u'\sim _{\mathcal I}v+v',\qquad a u\sim _{\mathcal I}a v\quad (a>0).  \] Proof. Fix a coordinate neighborhood $U\subset X$ and a modification $\pi :Y	o U$ with smooth source. At every $y\in Y$, the elementary rules for the Lelong numbers of maxima, sums and positive multiples give \[   egin{aligned}  
u (\max (u,u')\circ \pi ,y) & =\min \{ 
u (u\circ \pi ,y),
u (u'\circ \pi ,y)\} ,\  
u ((u+u')\circ \pi ,y) & =
u (u\circ \pi ,y)+
u (u'\circ \pi ,y),\  
u (a u\circ \pi ,y)& =a
u (u\circ \pi ,y). \end{aligned}  \] These rules are unaffected by smooth local corrections. Since $u\sim _{\mathcal I}v$ and $u'\sim _{\mathcal I}v'$, the first item of theorem 5.37.3 shows that the right-hand sides do not change when $u,u'$ are replaced by $v,v'$. The converse direction of the same item, applied on each coordinate neighborhood, gives the three asserted equivalences. For the cancellation rule, suppose that $u+h\sim _{\mathcal I}v+h$. By the first item of theorem 5.37.3 , the pullbacks $(u+h)\circ \pi $ and $(v+h)\circ \pi $ have the same Lelong numbers. The common summand $h\circ \pi $ is quasi-plurisubharmonic, so its Lelong numbers are finite, and subtracting them shows that $u\circ \pi $ and $v\circ \pi $ have the same Lelong numbers. Hence $u\sim _{\mathcal I}v$ by the same item. The reverse implication is the addition rule proved above. $\square$

title: Lemma 5.37.5
text: Lemma 5.37.5 . 5929CFA4B87F Let $q$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic on a complex manifold and suppose that $\nu (q,x)=0$ at every point. Then $\mathrm e^{-tq}$ is locally integrable for every $t>0$. For every quasi-plurisubharmonic $v$ and every $t>0$, \[  \mathcal I\bigl (t(v+q)\bigr )=\mathcal I(tv).  \] Proof. Fix a point $x$ and add a smooth correction to make $q$ plurisubharmonic on a bounded pseudoconvex coordinate neighborhood. Form the weighted Bergman space of proposition 5.35.1 at weight $t$. If every member vanished at $x$, the Cauchy estimates, together with the local upper bound for $q$, would give \[  \sup _{\| g\| _ t\leq 1}|g(z)|\leq C|z-x|  \] near $x$. Its Bergman potential would consequently have Lelong number at least $1/t$, contradicting ( 5.35.3 ). There is therefore a weighted square-integrable holomorphic function nonzero at $x$. On a smaller neighborhood it is bounded away from zero, so its weighted norm proves integrability of $\mathrm e^{-tq}$. Smooth corrections do not change this conclusion. Thus $q\sim _{\mathcal I}0$; the addition rule in lemma 5.37.4 gives $v+q\sim _{\mathcal I}v$, which is precisely the asserted equality at every weight. $\square$
