title: Lemma 5.37.7
text: Lemma 5.37.7 . 2FA053FE56D9 Let $p:Z\to Y$ be a holomorphic submersion of complex manifolds and let $u\in \mathrm{QPSH}(Y)$. For every $t>0$, \[  \mathcal I(tu\circ p) =\mathcal I(tu)\mathcal O_ Z.  \] Proof. Work in product coordinates $(z,\zeta )$ with $p(z,\zeta )=z$. Write $\alpha $ for a multi-index in the fiber variables and $\mathrm{d}\lambda _\zeta $ for their Euclidean volume. A germ in the ideal on the right is a finite sum of bounded holomorphic multiples of pullbacks of germs that are square integrable against $\mathrm{e}^{-tu(z)}$. Fubini's theorem shows that it is weighted-integrable on a sufficiently small product neighborhood. Conversely, let $F(z,\zeta )$ be a weighted-integrable holomorphic germ and expand it in the fiber variables, \[  F(z,\zeta )=\sum _\alpha f_\alpha (z)\zeta ^\alpha .  \] The coefficient estimate for a holomorphic function on a polydisk gives, on smaller product neighborhoods, \[  |f_\alpha (z)|^2\leq C_\alpha \int |F(z,\zeta )|^2\, \mathrm{d}\lambda _\zeta .  \] Multiplying by $\mathrm{e}^{-tu(z)}$ and integrating in $z$ shows that each coefficient germ $f_\alpha $ belongs to $\mathcal I(tu)$. Let $J$ be the extension of this ideal to the local ring $R$ of holomorphic germs on the product. Every finite Taylor sum of $F$ belongs to $J$, and the remainder of total fiber degree at least $N$ belongs to $(\zeta )^ N$. Thus the class of $F$ in $R/J$ lies in $(\zeta )^ N(R/J)$ for every $N$. By the Krull intersection theorem for the finitely generated module $R/J$ over the Noetherian local ring $R$, the intersection of these submodules is zero. Hence $F\in J$. Smooth corrections and smooth positive volume densities do not change the integrability conditions. $\square$

title: Example 5.37.8
text: Example 5.37.8 . E39EAA145A67 Exact multiplier-ideal pullback can fail at a critical fiber. On a polydisk in $\mathbb C^ n$, $n\geq 1$, let $f(z_0,\ldots ,z_{n-1})=z_0^2$ and put $v(t)=\tfrac 12\log |t|^2$. At the origin, \[  \mathcal I(v)=\mathcal O,\qquad \mathcal I(v\circ f)=(z_0) \ne \mathcal I(v)\mathcal O.  \] Proof. On the curve the coefficient is $1/2$, so the multiplier ideal is the zeroth power of the maximal ideal. Upstairs $v\circ f=\log |z_0|^2$ has coefficient one along the smooth divisor $\{ z_0=0\} $. Apply lemma 5.37.1 in codimension one to get its first ideal power. $\square$

title: 5.37.9 Weighted distance from a sum of multiplier ideals
search_title: Weighted distance from a sum of multiplier ideals
text: Membership in a multiplier ideal is a local integrability condition. On a pseudoconvex domain one can ask, more quantitatively, how small the weighted norm of a holomorphic function can be made by subtracting global sections of such ideals. A sharp $L^2$ estimate answers this question for one weight. Applied successively, with the remaining weights kept in the auxiliary weight at each step, it gives a product bound for several weights. Throughout this subsection, $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$ is a pseudoconvex domain, $n\geq 1$, and $\mathrm{d}V$ denotes Euclidean volume. For a plurisubharmonic weight $\rho $ on $\Omega $, put \[  \| f\| _\rho ^2=\int _\Omega |f|^2\mathrm e^{-\rho }\, \mathrm{d}V.  \] For a plurisubharmonic function $v$ on $\Omega $, we write $\Gamma (\Omega ,\mathcal I(v))$ for the space of holomorphic functions on $\Omega $ whose germs belong to $\mathcal I(v)$ at every point. Membership requires only local weighted integrability, not a finite global norm. We first prove a division estimate with two summands. Its sharp constant comes from keeping the full sum of the twisting functions in the $\bar\partial $-estimate. Lemma 5.37.10 . 95217B5924C0 Let $\psi ,\phi _1,\phi _2$ be plurisubharmonic functions on $\Omega $, and suppose that $S=\mathrm e^{\phi _1}+\mathrm e^{\phi _2}<1$. If $f$ is holomorphic and \[  J=\int _\Omega \frac{|f|^2\mathrm e^{-\psi }}{S^2}\, \mathrm{d}V<+\infty ,  \] then there are holomorphic $F_1,F_2$ with $F_1+F_2=f$ and 363923246C67 5.37.11 \begin{equation}  \int _\Omega \bigl (|F_1|^2\mathrm e^{-\phi _1} +|F_2|^2\mathrm e^{-\phi _2}\bigr ) \mathrm e^{-\psi }\, \mathrm{d}V\leq J. \end{equation} Proof. Step 1: a twisted $\bar\partial $-estimate. Suppose first that $\Omega $ is bounded, that the weights are smooth on a neighborhood of $\overline\Omega $ with $S<1$ there, and that $\Phi =\log S$ is strictly plurisubharmonic. Set $\chi =\phi _1+\phi _2+\psi $ and $A=(\Phi _{j\bar k})$. For a $(0,1)$-form $b$, write $|b|_ A^2$ for its squared norm with respect to the dual of this positive Hermitian matrix. We claim that every $\bar\partial $-closed $(0,1)$-form $b$ for which the right-hand side below is finite admits a solution $u$ of 35D5D6699C73 5.37.12 \begin{equation}  \bar\partial u=b,\qquad \int |u|^2\mathrm e^{\Phi -\chi }\, \mathrm{d}V \leq \int (1-\mathrm e^\Phi )|b|_ A^2 \mathrm e^{-\chi }\, \mathrm{d}V. \end{equation} To prove this, define for $x<0$ \[  T(x)=-\log (1-\mathrm e^ x),\qquad \eta (x)=\frac{-x}{1-\mathrm e^ x}-1,\qquad \lambda (x)=-\frac{\eta '(x)}{T'(x)}.  \] The inequality $-x>1-\mathrm e^ x$ gives $\eta >0$. Also $\eta '= -[1-(1-x)\mathrm e^ x]/(1-\mathrm e^ x)^2<0$, whereas $T'>0$, so $\lambda >0$. Direct differentiation gives \[  \eta T'-\eta '=1,\qquad \eta T''-\eta ''-\frac{(\eta ')^2}{\lambda }=0,\qquad \frac{\mathrm e^{-T}}{\eta +\lambda }=\mathrm e^ x.  \] Use the weight $h=\mathrm e^{-\chi -T(\Phi )}$ on the trivial line bundle and evaluate the twisting functions at $\Phi $. The twisted curvature is \[  \begin{aligned}  B_0& =\eta \, \mathrm i\partial \bar\partial (\chi +T(\Phi )) -\mathrm i\partial \bar\partial \eta -\mathrm i\lambda ^{-1}\partial \eta \wedge \bar\partial \eta \\ & =\eta \, \mathrm i\partial \bar\partial \chi +\mathrm i\partial \bar\partial \Phi \geq \mathrm i\partial \bar\partial \Phi . \end{aligned}  \] Let $\Lambda $ denote contraction by the Euclidean Kähler form and $\bar\partial _ h^*$ the weighted adjoint. For a compactly supported $(n,1)$-form $v$, the twisted Bochner identity and the weighted Cauchy–Schwarz inequality give 04CF8B360946 5.37.13 \begin{equation}  \langle [B_0,\Lambda ]v,v\rangle _ h \leq \| \sqrt{\eta +\lambda }\, \bar\partial _ h^*v\| _ h^2 +\| \sqrt\eta \, \bar\partial v\| _ h^2. \end{equation} More explicitly, the cross term is bounded by $\lambda |\bar\partial _ h^*v|^2+\lambda ^{-1}|(\bar\partial \eta )^*v|^2$; the latter term is exactly the commutator contribution of $\mathrm i\lambda ^{-1}\partial \eta \wedge \bar\partial \eta $. The terms of type $(n+1,1)$ vanish, and the remaining connection norm has a favorable sign. The Hilbert space existence argument applied to ( 5.37.13 ) therefore gives \[  \int \frac{|u|^2h}{\eta +\lambda }\, \mathrm{d}V \leq \int |b|_ A^2h\, \mathrm{d}V.  \] To see the coefficient, project a test form to $\ker \bar\partial $. On this kernel the second term of ( 5.37.13 ) vanishes, and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality in the curvature norm bounds the functional $v\mapsto \langle b,v\rangle _ h$ by $(\int |b|_ A^2h)^{1/2}\| \sqrt{\eta +\lambda }\, \bar\partial _ h^*v\| _ h$. The Riesz representation theorem gives a solution with the asserted norm. The twisting functions are bounded on $\Omega $, since $\Phi $ is smooth and bounded away from both $-\infty $ and $0$. The argument first uses a complete Kähler metric; approximating the Euclidean metric by the Euclidean metric plus small positive multiples of a complete metric gives the Euclidean statement. Under the identification with canonical-bundle-valued forms, the $(n,0)$ norm integral and the curvature-dual $(n,1)$ integral have the same coordinate expressions as above. Since $h=\mathrm e^{-\chi }(1-\mathrm e^\Phi )$, the identities for $T,\eta ,\lambda $ now give ( 5.37.12 ). Step 2: division for smooth weights. Put $v_ i=\mathrm e^{\phi _ i}/S$ and $\ell =(v_1f,v_2f)$. Equip $\mathbb C^2$ with the diagonal metric $(\mathrm e^{-\phi _1},\mathrm e^{-\phi _2})$. Then $\ell $ is orthogonal to the kernel line of the sum map, generated by $(1,-1)$, and $|\ell |^2=|f|^2/S$. Write $\delta =\phi _1-\phi _2$. The Hessian formula gives \[  \begin{aligned}  A& =v_1(\phi _{1,j\bar k})+v_2(\phi _{2,j\bar k}) +v_1v_2(\delta _ j\overline{\delta _ k}),\\  \bar\partial (v_1f)& =fv_1v_2\bar\partial \delta . \end{aligned}  \] Thus $v_1v_2|\bar\partial \delta |_ A^2\leq 1$ and, for $b=\bar\partial (v_1f)$, \[  |b|_ A^2\mathrm e^{-\chi } \leq \frac{|f|^2\mathrm e^{-\psi }}{S^2}.  \] Solve ( 5.37.12 ) for this $b$ and set $F=\ell -u(1,-1)$. Since $v_1+v_2=1$, the vector $F=(F_1,F_2)$ is holomorphic and its components sum to $f$. The squared norm of $(1,-1)$ is $\mathrm e^{-\phi _1}+\mathrm e^{-\phi _2}=S\mathrm e^{-\phi _1-\phi _2}$. Orthogonality and ( 5.37.12 ) consequently give \[  \begin{aligned}  \int |F|^2\mathrm e^{-\psi } & =\int \frac{|f|^2\mathrm e^{-\psi }}{S} +\int |u|^2\mathrm e^{\Phi -\chi }\\ & \leq \int \frac{|f|^2\mathrm e^{-\psi }}{S^2}. \end{aligned}  \] This proves ( 5.37.11 ) for smooth weights. Step 3: general weights. Exhaust $\Omega $ by bounded pseudoconvex domains with compact closures in $\Omega $. On each of them, convolve the weights on a slightly larger neighborhood and add a sufficiently small positive multiple of $|z|^2$. These smooth plurisubharmonic weights dominate the original weights, converge to them almost everywhere, preserve $S<1$ on the chosen closure, and make $\Phi $ strictly plurisubharmonic. The corresponding integrals $J$ are bounded by the original one. On every compact subset the weights have common upper bounds, so ( 5.37.11 ) gives uniform unweighted local $L^2$ bounds for both components. The holomorphic mean-value inequality and a diagonal extraction give holomorphic limits. Almost-everywhere convergence of the weights and Fatou's lemma yield ( 5.37.11 ) on $\Omega $, and $F_1+F_2=f$ passes to the limit. $\square$ Proposition 5.37.14 . B929E98153F2 Let $\psi $ and $\phi $ be plurisubharmonic functions on $\Omega $ with $\phi <0$, and let $p>1$. For holomorphic $f$ with $I=\| f\| _{\psi +\phi }^2<+\infty $, define \[  c=\inf \{ \| g\| _\psi ^2:g\in \mathcal O(\Omega ),\quad f-g\in \Gamma (\Omega ,\mathcal I(p\phi +\psi ))\} .  \] Then $c\leq (1-1/p)I$. Proof. For $t>0$, apply lemma 5.37.10 with \[  \phi _1=\log \frac{t}{1+t}+p\phi ,\qquad \phi _2=-\log (1+t).  \] Their exponential sum is $S=(1+t\mathrm e^{p\phi })/(1+t)<1$. The integral $J$ of the lemma is finite, since $\| f\| _\psi ^2\leq I$ and $S\geq 1/(1+t)$. The first component $F_1$ belongs to $\Gamma (\Omega ,\mathcal I(p\phi +\psi ))$, so the second component $F_2=f-F_1$ is admissible for $c$, and the norm estimate gives \[  \frac{c}{1+t}\leq \int _\Omega \frac{|f|^2\mathrm e^{-\psi }}{(1+t\mathrm e^{p\phi })^2}\, \mathrm{d}V.  \] Set $t=x^ p$ and integrate over $x>0$. With $\kappa _ k=\int _0^\infty (1+x^ p)^{-k}\, \mathrm{d}x$, Tonelli's theorem and the change of variable $x\mapsto x\mathrm e^\phi $ give $c\kappa _1\leq I\kappa _2$; the pole set of $\phi $ is Lebesgue null. Since $p>1$, both integrals are finite, and integrating the derivative of $x/(1+x^ p)$ over $(0,\infty )$ gives $\kappa _2=(1-1/p)\kappa _1$. The argument does not require the infimum to be attained. $\square$ Theorem 5.37.15 . 5433D9F2E00C Let $\psi $ and $\phi _1,\ldots ,\phi _ r$ be plurisubharmonic functions on $\Omega $, with $r\geq 1$ and $\phi _ i<0$, and choose $p_ i>1$. For holomorphic $f$ with \[  I=\| f\| _{\psi +\sum _ i\phi _ i}^2<+\infty ,  \] put \[  c=\inf \left\{ \| g\| _\psi ^2:g\in \mathcal O(\Omega ),\quad f-g\in \sum _{i=1}^ r\Gamma (\Omega ,\mathcal I(p_ i\phi _ i+\psi ))\right\} .  \] Then 646E9C7EF985 5.37.16 \begin{equation}  c\leq \prod _{i=1}^ r\left(1-\frac1{p_ i}\right)I. \end{equation} For $r\leq n$, this constant is optimal for the stated class of data. Proof. Set $\psi _ i=\psi +\sum _{j>i}\phi _ j$, $a_ i=1-1/p_ i$, and $f_0=f$. For arbitrary $\varepsilon _ i>0$, proposition 5.37.14 successively gives holomorphic $f_ i$ such that \[  \begin{aligned}  \| f_ i\| _{\psi _ i}^2& \leq a_ i\| f_{i-1}\| _{\psi _ i+\phi _ i}^2+\varepsilon _ i,\\  f_{i-1}-f_ i& \in \Gamma (\Omega ,\mathcal I(p_ i\phi _ i+\psi _ i)). \end{aligned}  \] Since $\psi _ i\leq \psi $, these ideals are contained in $\mathcal I(p_ i\phi _ i+\psi )$. As $f-f_ r$ is the sum of the differences $f_{i-1}-f_ i$, the function $f_ r$ is admissible for $c$. Moreover, $\psi _ i+\phi _ i=\psi _{i-1}$ for $i\geq 1$ and $\psi _ r=\psi $, so iteration gives \[  c\leq \left(\prod _ i a_ i\right)I +\sum _{i=1}^ r\varepsilon _ i\prod _{j>i}a_ j.  \] Letting every $\varepsilon _ i$ tend to zero proves ( 5.37.16 ). For sharpness when $r\leq n$, take the unit polydisk $\Omega =\Delta ^ n$, $f=1$, $\psi =0$, and $\phi _ i=p_ i^{-1}\log |z_ i|^2$ for $i\leq r$. By lemma 5.37.1 , $\mathcal I(p_ i\phi _ i)=(z_ i)$. Every admissible $g$ equals one on $Y=\{ z_1=\cdots =z_ r=0\} $, hence $g(0)=1$. Orthogonality of the monomials on the polydisk gives $\| g\| _0^2\geq \pi ^ n$, with equality for $g=1$. Direct radial integration gives $I=\pi ^ n\prod _ i p_ i/(p_ i-1)$, so equality holds in ( 5.37.16 ). $\square$ The congruence condition in theorem 5.37.15 involves a sum of global sections, and the successive remainders in its proof are global; a condition on a single germ would not produce them. The estimate holds for any number of weights, whereas the optimality assertion uses distinct coordinate directions and therefore requires $r\leq n$.

title: 5.37.24 Distance for several hyperplane weights
text: In this subsection, $n\geq 2$, $B\subset \mathbb C^ n$ is the unit ball, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is Euclidean volume. If the weights have logarithmic poles along several hyperplanes through the origin, every admissible remainder must take a prescribed value at their common zero. On the other hand, the input norm stays finite as long as the combined radial exponent is below the dimension. Together these observations give a positive distance even in part of the range where the planar distance of theorem 5.37.22 vanishes. Example 5.37.25 . 9F227CC9F378 Fix $r>n$ and $p>r/n$. There are negative plurisubharmonic functions $\phi _1,\ldots ,\phi _ r$ on $B$ for which \[  I=\int _ B\mathrm e^{-\sum _ i\phi _ i}\, \mathrm{d}V<+\infty  \] and 4F7B8ACF0243 5.37.26 \begin{equation}  \inf \left\{ \int _ B|g|^2\, \mathrm{d}V:g\in \mathcal O(B),\quad 1-g\in \sum _{i=1}^ r\Gamma (B,\mathcal I(p\phi _ i))\right\}  =\frac{\pi ^ n}{n!}>0. \end{equation} In particular, for $r/n<p\leq r$, the distance is positive although $\sum _ i1/p=r/p\geq 1$. Proof. Choose distinct real numbers $t_1,\ldots ,t_ r$ and unit linear forms \[  \ell _ i(z)=\frac{\sum _{k=0}^{n-1}t_ i^ kz_{k+1}}{(\sum _{k=0}^{n-1}t_ i^{2k})^{1/2}}.  \] Any $n$ of these forms are linearly independent, since the determinant of their unnormalized coefficients is a nonzero Vandermonde determinant. Put $\phi _ i=p^{-1}\log |\ell _ i|^2$. Since the coefficient vectors of the $\ell _ i$ have norm one, $|\ell _ i(z)|<1$ on $B$, so the $\phi _ i$ are negative plurisubharmonic functions. By lemma 5.37.1 , $\mathcal I(p\phi _ i)=(\ell _ i)$. At a nonzero point, at most $n-1$ of the forms vanish. These forms are linearly independent and can be used as part of a holomorphic coordinate system, while the other forms are bounded away from zero on a small neighborhood of the point. Hence \[  W(z)=\prod _{i=1}^ r|\ell _ i(z)|^{-2/p}  \] is locally integrable off the origin, because each factor $|\ell _ i|^{-2/p}$ has exponent $2/p<2$ (note that $p>r/n>1$). By compactness, $W$ is integrable on every closed annulus. Set $s=r/p$ and let $\mathrm{d}\sigma $ denote surface measure on the unit sphere. Homogeneity and polar integration over such an annulus show that \[  A=\int _{|\zeta |=1}\prod _ i|\ell _ i(\zeta )|^{-2/p}\,  \mathrm{d}\sigma (\zeta )<+\infty .  \] Tonelli then gives \[  I=A\int _0^1\rho ^{2n-1-2s}\, \mathrm{d}\rho =\frac{A}{2(n-s)}<+\infty ,  \] since $s<n$. This takes care of the common zero at the origin as well as of the individual hyperplanes. Every global section of $(\ell _ i)$ vanishes at the origin. Thus every admissible $g$ in ( 5.37.26 ) satisfies $g(0)=1$. For each $z\in B$, the holomorphic function $\lambda \mapsto g(\lambda z)$ is defined on a disk of radius greater than one, and the submean inequality for the subharmonic function $|g(\lambda z)|^2$ gives \[  \frac1{2\pi }\int _0^{2\pi }|g(\mathrm e^{\mathrm i\tau }z)|^2\,  \mathrm{d}\tau \geq |g(0)|^2=1.  \] Integrating in $z$ and using the rotation invariance of $B$ proves $\int _ B|g|^2\, \mathrm{d}V\geq \operatorname {Vol}(B)=\pi ^ n/n!$, also when the integral is infinite. The constant $g=1$ is admissible and attains this bound. $\square$ Hence, for these equal exponents, the optimal universal constant in an estimate of the distance by a multiple of $I$ is at least $\pi ^ n/(n!I)>0$. In particular, the vanishing of the optimal constant for $s\geq 1$ in theorem 5.37.22 does not extend to higher dimensions. The example does not determine the optimal constant for $r>n$.

Put $\phi _ i=p^{-1}\log |\ell _ i|^2$. Since the coefficient vectors of the $\ell _ i$ have norm one, $|\ell _ i(z)|<1$ on $B$, so the $\phi _ i$ are negative plurisubharmonic functions. By lemma 5.37.1 , $\mathcal I(p\phi _ i)=(\ell _ i)$. At a nonzero point, at most $n-1$ of the forms vanish. These forms are linearly independent and can be used as part of a holomorphic coordinate system, while the other forms are bounded away from zero on a small neighborhood of the point. Hence \[  W(z)=\prod _{i=1}^ r|\ell _ i(z)|^{-2/p}  \] is locally integrable off the origin, because each factor $|\ell _ i|^{-2/p}$ has exponent $2/p<2$ (note that $p>r/n>1$). By compactness, $W$ is integrable on every closed annulus. Set $s=r/p$ and let $\mathrm{d}\sigma $ denote surface measure on the unit sphere. Homogeneity and polar integration over such an annulus show that \[  A=\int _{|\zeta |=1}\prod _ i|\ell _ i(\zeta )|^{-2/p}\,  \mathrm{d}\sigma (\zeta )<+\infty .  \] Tonelli then gives \[  I=A\int _0^1\rho ^{2n-1-2s}\, \mathrm{d}\rho =\frac{A}{2(n-s)}<+\infty ,  \] since $s<n$. This takes care of the common zero at the origin as well as of the individual hyperplanes. Every global section of $(\ell _ i)$ vanishes at the origin. Thus every admissible $g$ in ( 5.37.26 ) satisfies $g(0)=1$. For each $z\in B$, the holomorphic function $\lambda \mapsto g(\lambda z)$ is defined on a disk of radius greater than one, and the submean inequality for the subharmonic function $|g(\lambda z)|^2$ gives \[  \frac1{2\pi }\int _0^{2\pi }|g(\mathrm e^{\mathrm i\tau }z)|^2\,  \mathrm{d}\tau \geq |g(0)|^2=1.  \] Integrating in $z$ and using the rotation invariance of $B$ proves $\int _ B|g|^2\, \mathrm{d}V\geq \operatorname {Vol}(B)=\pi ^ n/n!$, also when the integral is infinite. The constant $g=1$ is admissible and attains this bound. $\square$

title: Equation 5.37.26
text: 4F7B8ACF0243 5.37.26 \begin{equation}  \inf \left\{ \int _ B|g|^2\, \mathrm{d}V:g\in \mathcal O(B),\quad 1-g\in \sum _{i=1}^ r\Gamma (B,\mathcal I(p\phi _ i))\right\}  =\frac{\pi ^ n}{n!}>0. \end{equation}

title: 5.38 Lelong numbers and divisorial estimates
text:
Lelong numbers measure the logarithmic concentration of a positive current. Along a divisor, a lower bound for the generic Lelong number allows us to subtract the corresponding multiple of the divisor without losing positivity. At points, the local mass formula controls Lelong numbers under convergence and uniformly in a fixed background. For a prime divisor $E$ on a complex manifold, $[E]$ denotes its current of integration, and $
u (w,E)$ is the generic Lelong number along $E$ of a quasi-plurisubharmonic function $w$, as defined in section 5.34 . We use the following local consequence of Siu's decomposition theorem, recalled in Theorem 10.4.8 (Siu's divisorial decomposition) and . If $T$ is a closed positive $(1,1)$-current and $E$ is a prime divisor, the restriction of (the coefficient measures of) $T$ to $E$ equals the generic Lelong number of $T$ along $E$ times $[E]$. In particular, removing finitely many of these divisorial components from $T$ leaves a positive current. Distinct prime divisors do not contribute overlapping mass, since their intersections have codimension at least two. All these are local statements about closed currents. Lemma 5.38.1 . 3AA98220C897 Let $M$ be a complex manifold, let $ eta $ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $M$, let $w\in \mathrm{PSH}(M, eta )$, and let $E_1,\ldots ,E_ N$ be distinct prime divisors on $M$, with $N\geq 1$. Then \[   eta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w-\sum _{j=1}^ N
u (w,E_ j)[E_ j]\geq 0.  \] The form $ eta $ need not be closed. Proof. Work on a coordinate ball and choose a smooth function $ho $ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}ho \geq  eta $. The current \[  T=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w+ho )=( eta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)+(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}ho - eta )  \] is closed and positive. A smooth form, viewed through its coefficient measures, assigns zero mass to every proper analytic set. Thus $T$ and $ eta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w$ have the same restriction to $ igcup _ jE_ j$, and the consequence of Siu's theorem stated above identifies this restriction with $\sum _ j
u (w,E_ j)[E_ j]$. Subtracting it from the positive current $ eta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w$ leaves the restriction of $ eta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w$ to the complement of $ igcup _ jE_ j$, which is positive. This proves the inequality locally, hence globally. Note that $ eta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w$ itself need not be closed. $\square$ Order makes the support theorem a rigidity statement for potentials: two ordered quasi-plurisubharmonic functions whose Hessians agree outside an analytic set already differ by a constant. Lemma 5.38.2 . 4296DE167374 Let $u\leq v$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic on a connected compact complex manifold $X$, and let $Z\subsetneq X$ be analytic. If $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v$ on $X\setminus Z$, then $v=u+C$ for a real constant $C$. Proof. The current $S=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v-u)$ is real, closed, of order zero and supported on $Z$. By the support theorem in [ Chapter III, Corollaries 2.11 and 2.14, pp. 141–143 , DemCADG ] , 3B6E06712331 5.38.3  egin{equation}  S=\sum _{j=1}^ m c_ j[Z_ j],\qquad c_ j=
u (v,Z_ j)-
u (u,Z_ j)\leq 0, \end{equation} where $Z_ j$ are the prime divisorial components of $Z$. Indeed, the support theorem first gives real constants $c_ j$ such that $S-\sum _ jc_ j[Z_ j]$ is supported in codimension at least two; this closed current of order zero then vanishes by the same theorem. Near a generic smooth point of $Z_ j$, with local equation $z_1=0$, the function $v-u-c_ j\log |z_1|^2$ has zero complex Hessian and is therefore smooth and pluriharmonic. This identifies $c_ j$ with the difference of the generic Lelong numbers, and $c_ j\leq 0$ because $u\leq v$. Thus $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u-v)=-S\geq 0$. Hence the locally integrable distribution $u-v$ has a global plurisubharmonic representative, which is constant by the maximum principle on the compact connected manifold $X$. Since quasi-plurisubharmonic functions that agree almost everywhere agree everywhere, $v=u+C$ for a constant $C$. $\square$ Every closed real $(1,1)$-current is the sum of a smooth closed form and the complex Hessian of a global distribution, and positivity of the current makes this potential quasi-plurisubharmonic. This decomposition allows us to attach an ordinary singularity type to a divisorial current. Lemma 5.38.4 . 7A2D4C65C667 Let $Z$ be a complex manifold and $T$ a closed real $(1,1)$-current on $Z$. There are a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $ eta $ and a real distribution $v$ such that \[  T= eta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v.  \] If $T\geq 0$, then $v$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic. Any two distributional potentials in such decompositions differ by a smooth function. Proof. The local $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$-Poincaré lemma gives real distributional potentials $v_ i$ on the sets of a cover of $Z$ by coordinate neighborhoods, with $T=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ i$; for positive $T$ these potentials are plurisubharmonic. See [ Chapter III, Section 1.18 and Proposition 1.19 , DemCADG ] . On overlaps $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v_ i-v_ j)=0$. Taking the Euclidean trace shows that $v_ i-v_ j$ is a harmonic distribution, so it is smooth by elliptic regularity. Choose a smooth locally finite partition of unity $(\chi _ i)$ subordinate to the cover and put $v=\sum _ i\chi _ i v_ i$, each term being extended by zero as a distribution. On the $j$th neighborhood, \[  v-v_ j=\sum _ i\chi _ i(v_ i-v_ j)  \] is smooth. Thus $ eta =T-\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v=-\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v-v_ j)$ is smooth on each neighborhood, hence on $Z$, and it is real and closed. For positive $T$, the same identity expresses $v$ locally as a plurisubharmonic function plus a smooth function. Finally, if $T= eta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v= eta '+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v'$ are two such decompositions, then $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v-v')= eta '- eta $ is smooth; taking a smooth Hermitian trace and applying elliptic regularity shows that $v-v'$ is smooth. $\square$ For a potential whose complex Hessian is a divisorial current minus a smooth form, ordinary domination, ideal domination and the corresponding inequalities for generic Lelong numbers along the divisors are all equivalent. Countably many divisors are allowed, provided the divisorial current has finite mass. Lemma 5.38.5 . 65C35F77CB06 Let $Y$ be a connected compact complex manifold. Let $(D_ j)$ be a finite or countable family of distinct prime divisors on $Y$ and $c_ j>0$ real coefficients such that $S=\sum _ jc_ j[D_ j]$ is a positive current of finite mass, and let $ eta $ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $Y$. Let $v\in \mathrm{QPSH}(Y)$ satisfy \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v=S- eta .  \] Then, for $a\in \mathrm{QPSH}(Y)$, the following conditions are equivalent: \[  a\preceq v,\qquad a\preceq _{\mathcal I}v,\qquad 
u (a,D_ j)\geq c_ j\quad \hbox{for every }j.  \] Proof. We first note that $
u (v,D_ j)=c_ j$. Indeed, the restriction of $S$ to $D_ j$ is $c_ j[D_ j]$: distinct divisors intersect in codimension at least two, and such sets carry no mass of any divisor current, also after countable summation. Smooth forms give every divisor zero mass. The local form of Siu's decomposition, applied after a smooth correction, therefore gives $
u (v,D_ j)=c_ j$. Ordinary domination implies ideal domination by proposition 5.33.2 , and ideal domination implies the asserted inequalities for generic Lelong numbers by theorem 5.37.3 . It remains to prove that these inequalities imply ordinary domination. Choose a Hermitian form $\Lambda $ with $a\in \mathrm{PSH}(Y,\Lambda )$. By lemma 5.38.1 and the inequalities $
u (a,D_ j)\geq c_ j$, each finite partial sum of $S$ can be subtracted from $\Lambda +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a$ without losing positivity. Letting the partial sums increase to $S$ gives \[  \Lambda +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a-S\geq 0.  \] Consequently $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(a-v)\geq  eta -\Lambda $. Hence the integrable function $a-v$ has a quasi-plurisubharmonic representative, which is bounded above on the compact manifold $Y$. This yields $a\leq v+C$ almost everywhere, and lemma 5.24.3 extends this inequality everywhere. Thus $a\preceq v$. $\square$ Together, the two preceding lemmas attach a canonical ordinary singularity type to a countable divisorial current of finite mass. Corollary 5.38.6 . F5277854ECB3 Let $Z$ be a connected compact complex manifold, let $(D_ j)$ be a finite or countable family of distinct prime divisors on $Z$, and let $c_ j>0$. Suppose that $S=\sum _ jc_ j[D_ j]$ is a closed positive current of finite mass. Then there are quasi-plurisubharmonic functions $v$ on $Z$ satisfying \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v=S- eta  \] for a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $ eta $, and any two such functions differ by a smooth function. In particular, they determine a canonical ordinary singularity type, which depends only on $S$. Proof. Lemma 5.38.4 , applied to $T=S$, gives the decomposition, with $v$ quasi-plurisubharmonic since $S\geq 0$, and shows that any two such potentials differ by a smooth function. By proposition 5.33.1 , they have the same ordinary singularity type. $\square$ Lemma 5.38.7 . E04E4D6C502E Let $u_ j,u$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on a complex manifold with a common smooth lower curvature bound, that is, $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j\geq - eta $ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\geq - eta $ for one smooth real $(1,1)$-form $ eta $. If $u_ j	o u$ in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$, then at every point $x$, \[  
u (u,x)\geq \limsup _ j
u (u_ j,x).  \] Proof. On a coordinate ball about $x$, add one smooth function to all the potentials to make them plurisubharmonic, and write $p_ j,p$ for the resulting functions. Let $n$ be the dimension and $\kappa $ the Euclidean form of the chart. Distributional convergence gives weak convergence of the positive trace measures $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p_ j\wedge \kappa ^{n-1}$ to $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p\wedge \kappa ^{n-1}$. For every sufficiently small radius $r$ such that the sphere of radius $r$ about $x$ has zero mass for the limit measure, the masses of the balls converge. The Lelong monotonicity formula bounds each $
u (p_ j,x)$ by the normalized trace mass of $p_ j$ on such a ball. Taking the upper limit in $j$, and then letting these radii decrease to zero, gives $\limsup _ j
u (p_ j,x)\leq 
u (p,x)$. Since smooth additions do not change Lelong numbers, this proves the lemma. $\square$ Lemma 5.38.8 . 1792691862B8 Let $Z$ be a connected compact complex manifold and let $ eta $ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form. There is a finite constant $C_ eta $ such that \[  
u (v,z)\leq C_ eta \qquad 	ext{for every }v\in \mathrm{PSH}(Z, eta )	ext{ and every }z\in Z.  \] In particular, the generic Lelong numbers of all $v\in \mathrm{PSH}(Z, eta )$ along all prime divisors are bounded by $C_ eta $. No normalization of the potentials is needed. Proof. Since adding a constant does not change Lelong numbers, we may assume that $\sup _ Zv=0$. By theorem 5.25.2 , these normalized potentials have a common $L^1$ bound. Cover $Z$ by finitely many triples of concentric coordinate balls, a smaller, an intermediate and a larger one, such that the smaller balls cover $Z$. On each larger ball choose a fixed smooth quadratic function $r$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}r\geq  eta $, so that $p=v+r$ is plurisubharmonic there. The functions $p$ obtained in this way have uniformly bounded local $L^1$ norms. Write $d=\dim Z$ and let $\kappa $ be the Euclidean form in the chart. Choose a nonnegative smooth cutoff $\chi $ supported in the larger ball and equal to one on an intermediate ball. Positivity and distributional integration by parts give \[  \int _{	ext{intermediate ball}}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p\wedge \kappa ^{d-1} \leq \int \chi \, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p\wedge \kappa ^{d-1} =\int p\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi \wedge \kappa ^{d-1} \leq C\| p\| _{L^1}.  \] Every point of the smaller ball is the center of a Euclidean ball of a fixed radius contained in the intermediate ball. The local Lelong monotonicity formula, recalled in Proposition 6.7.1 , bounds the Lelong number at this center by a fixed multiple of the trace mass of the intermediate ball. The finite cover gives one bound on $Z$. Since smooth additions and additive constants do not change Lelong numbers, this proves the assertion for the original potentials. $\square$ The Bergman estimates also control Lelong numbers on a fixed local modification. A local divisor over $X$ is a prime divisor $E$ on the source of a local modification $\pi :Z	o U$ of a coordinate neighborhood $U\subset X$, that is, a modification with smooth source $Z$. For a quasi-plurisubharmonic function $u$ on $X$, let $
u (u\circ \pi ,E)$ be the generic Lelong number of $u\circ \pi $ along $E$. For a holomorphic function or an ideal sheaf, $\operatorname {ord}_ E$ denotes the generic vanishing order along $E$ (for an ideal, the minimum of the orders of its local generators). Let $\operatorname {Jac}\pi $ be the holomorphic Jacobian determinant of $\pi $ in local coordinates. Write \[  
u _ E(u)=
u (u\circ \pi ,E),\qquad A_ U(E)=1+\operatorname {ord}_ E(\operatorname {Jac}\pi ).  \] The second number is the log discrepancy of $E$. Local modifications are not required to extend over the compact manifold. Lemma 5.38.9 . 1525C5219E69 For a quasi-plurisubharmonic function $u$ on $X$, every local divisor $E$ over $X$, and every real $m>0$, one has \[  \max \! \left\{ 
u _ E(u)- rac{A_ U(E)}m,0ight\}  \leq  rac1m\operatorname {ord}_ E\mathcal I(mu) \leq 
u _ E(u).  \] Here $\operatorname {ord}_ E\mathcal I(mu)$ is the order along $E$ of the pulled-back ideal. Consequently, if locally $a_ m=m^{-1}\log \sum _ k|f_{m,k}|^2+O(1)$, where the $f_{m,k}$ generate $\mathcal I(mu)$, then $
u _ E(a_ m)	o 
u _ E(u)$ as $m	o \infty $. Proof. The upper estimate follows from the local Bergman lower bound in proposition 5.35.1 : the logarithm of the sum of squared moduli of local generators of $\mathcal I(mu)$, divided by $m$, is at least $u$ up to a locally bounded term. Pulling back and taking generic Lelong numbers along $E$ reverses this inequality. For the lower estimate, take a local generator $f$ of the ideal and set $k=\operatorname {ord}_ E(f\circ \pi )$. Near a generic point of $E$, choose a local coordinate $z_1$ defining $E$. Divisorial removal (lemma 5.38.1 ), after a smooth correction, gives \[  u\circ \pi \leq 
u _ E(u)\log |z_1|^2+C.  \] Shrink around a point where the factors of $f\circ \pi $ and of the Jacobian complementary to the powers of $z_1$ do not vanish. The change-of-variables formula and local integrability of $|f|^2\mathrm{e}^{-mu}$ then require integrability in $z_1$ of \[  |z_1|^{2(k+A_ U(E)-1-m
u _ E(u))}.  \] This implies $k+A_ U(E)>m
u _ E(u)$, and in particular the weaker non-strict lower bound in the statement. Taking the minimum over a finite set of local generators and using that orders are nonnegative proves the lower estimate. Since $
u _ E(a_ m)=m^{-1}\operatorname {ord}_ E\mathcal I(mu)$, the last assertion follows by letting $m	o \infty $. $\square$ For rational $m>0$, the function $a_ m$ has analytic singularities in the sense of section 5.34 ; the estimate for real $m$ does not require this. Blowing up a point converts the divisorial estimate into a pointwise order bound on any local modification. Lemma 5.38.10 . 548A845099FB Let $U$ be a complex manifold of dimension $n$, let $u$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic on $U$, and let $\pi :Y	o U$ be a modification with smooth source. Fix $y\in Y$ and an integer $m\geq 1$. Write $J_\pi $ for the holomorphic Jacobian in local coordinates near $y$. If a nonzero holomorphic germ $g$ at $\pi (y)$ belongs to $\mathcal I(mu)$, then \[  \operatorname {ord}_ y(g\circ \pi ) \geq m
u (u\circ \pi ,y)-n-\operatorname {ord}_ yJ_\pi .  \] Proof. If $n\geq 2$, let $ho :\widetilde Y	o Y$ be the blowup of $y$ and let $E$ be its exceptional divisor. For $n=1$, take $ho $ to be the identity and $E=\{ y\} $. Set $F=\pi \circ ho $ and write $J_ F$ for its local holomorphic Jacobian determinant. Generic orders along $E$ give \[  
u (u\circ F,E)=
u (u\circ \pi ,y),\qquad \operatorname {ord}_ E(g\circ F)=\operatorname {ord}_ y(g\circ \pi ).  \] On a standard blowup chart the Jacobian of $ho $ has order $n-1$ along $E$. The chain rule therefore gives the log discrepancy over $U$ as \[  A_ U(E)=1+\operatorname {ord}_ E J_ F =n+\operatorname {ord}_ yJ_\pi .  \] Since $g\in \mathcal I(mu)$, the order of $g\circ F$ along $E$ is at least the order of this ideal. The lower estimate in lemma 5.38.9 , applied to $F$, therefore proves the inequality. $\square$ Lemma 5.38.11 . 1D91BF7CA736 Let $v$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic on $X$, and let $a$ have analytic singularities on $X$. If $v\preceq _{\mathcal I}a$, then $v\preceq a$. More precisely, it suffices to assume the finitely many inequalities \[  
u (v\circ \pi ,E)\geq 
u (a\circ \pi ,E)  \] for the prime components $E$ of the divisor obtained by principalizing, on one log resolution $\pi $, the ideal of an analytic presentation of $a$. Proof. Principalize the coherent ideal of an analytic presentation of $a$ by a log resolution $\pi :Y	o X$ with smooth $Y$. In suitable local coordinates $z_1,\ldots ,z_ n$ on $Y$, \[  a\circ \pi =\sum _{i=1}^ r b_ i\log |z_ i|^2+B, \qquad b_ i\geq 0,\qquad B\in L^\infty _{\mathrm{loc}},  \] where $r\leq n$. The finitely many inequalities in the statement give $
u (v\circ \pi ,\{ z_ i=0\} )\geq b_ i$; if $v\preceq _{\mathcal I}a$, these inequalities follow from theorem 5.37.3 . Add a smooth local function to $v\circ \pi $ to make it plurisubharmonic. Divisorial removal for this closed positive complex Hessian shows that \[  v\circ \pi -\sum _ i b_ i\log |z_ i|^2  \] has a quasi-plurisubharmonic representative; here the difference is first interpreted off the divisor, or as a locally integrable distribution. Such a representative is locally bounded above. Since $B$ is locally bounded, $v\circ \pi \leq a\circ \pi +C$ on each relatively compact chart of $Y$, away from the divisor. Since $\pi $ is proper, finitely many such charts cover the inverse image of a smaller coordinate neighborhood in $X$, which makes $C$ uniform there. Push the inequality down off the analytic exceptional set; as quasi-plurisubharmonic functions are determined by their values almost everywhere, it then holds everywhere. Finitely many neighborhoods cover the compact manifold, so $v\leq a+C$ globally. The only input from resolution of singularities is the principalization of a coherent ideal. Divisorial removal is applied to the closed positive complex Hessian obtained after a local smooth correction, so no closed background on $X$ is needed. $\square$ Lemma 5.38.12 . 3CF548646A75 Let $u,v$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic on $X$, and let $s$ have analytic singularities on $X$. Suppose that $u+v\leq s+O(1)$, and let $U_ m,V_ m$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic functions of analytic types $(1/m,\mathcal I(mu))$ and $(1/m,\mathcal I(mv))$. Then there are numbers $\delta _ m\downarrow 0$ such that \[  U_ m+V_ m\leq (1-\delta _ m)s+O(1) \quad \hbox{for all sufficiently large integers }m.  \] The bounded error may depend on $m$. Proof. If $s$ is bounded, upper bounds for $U_ m$ and $V_ m$ give the assertion with $\delta _ m=1/m$ for $m>1$. Otherwise principalize the ideal of $s$ by a log resolution $\pi :\widetilde X	o X$ with smooth $\widetilde X$. Let $E_ i$ be the components of the resulting divisor, with positive coefficients $c_ i$ in $s\circ \pi $; in local coordinates $z_ i$ defining these components, the singular part of $s\circ \pi $ is $\sum _ i c_ i\log |z_ i|^2$. Set $A_ i=1+\operatorname {ord}_{E_ i}(\operatorname {Jac}\pi )$. The hypothesis and lemma 5.38.9 give \[  
u (U_ m\circ \pi ,E_ i)+
u (V_ m\circ \pi ,E_ i) \geq 
u (u\circ \pi ,E_ i)+
u (v\circ \pi ,E_ i)- rac{2A_ i}{m} \geq c_ i- rac{2A_ i}{m}.  \] Choose a positive integer $N\geq \max _ i2A_ i/c_ i$ and put $\delta _ m=N/m$, which is less than one for large $m$. Then the right-hand side above is at least $(1-\delta _ m)c_ i$. After a smooth local correction, divisorial removal from the positive Hessian of $(U_ m+V_ m)\circ \pi $ shows that \[  (U_ m+V_ m)\circ \pi -(1-\delta _ m)\sum _ i c_ i\log |z_ i|^2  \] has a quasi-plurisubharmonic representative, which is locally bounded above. A finite cover of $\widetilde X$ by charts and descent along the proper map $\pi $, as in the proof of lemma 5.38.11 , therefore give $U_ m+V_ m\leq (1-\delta _ m)s+O(1)$. The bounded constant may depend on $m$. $\square$

title: Lemma 5.38.1
text: Lemma 5.38.1 . 3AA98220C897 Let $M$ be a complex manifold, let $\beta $ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $M$, let $w\in \mathrm{PSH}(M,\beta )$, and let $E_1,\ldots ,E_ N$ be distinct prime divisors on $M$, with $N\geq 1$. Then \[  \beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w-\sum _{j=1}^ N\nu (w,E_ j)[E_ j]\geq 0.  \] The form $\beta $ need not be closed. Proof. Work on a coordinate ball and choose a smooth function $\rho $ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho \geq \beta $. The current \[  T=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w+\rho )=(\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)+(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho -\beta )  \] is closed and positive. A smooth form, viewed through its coefficient measures, assigns zero mass to every proper analytic set. Thus $T$ and $\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w$ have the same restriction to $\bigcup _ jE_ j$, and the consequence of Siu's theorem stated above identifies this restriction with $\sum _ j\nu (w,E_ j)[E_ j]$. Subtracting it from the positive current $\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w$ leaves the restriction of $\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w$ to the complement of $\bigcup _ jE_ j$, which is positive. This proves the inequality locally, hence globally. Note that $\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w$ itself need not be closed. $\square$

title: Lemma 5.38.4
text: Lemma 5.38.4 . 7A2D4C65C667 Let $Z$ be a complex manifold and $T$ a closed real $(1,1)$-current on $Z$. There are a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $\beta $ and a real distribution $v$ such that \[  T=\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v.  \] If $T\geq 0$, then $v$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic. Any two distributional potentials in such decompositions differ by a smooth function. Proof. The local $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$-Poincaré lemma gives real distributional potentials $v_ i$ on the sets of a cover of $Z$ by coordinate neighborhoods, with $T=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ i$; for positive $T$ these potentials are plurisubharmonic. See [ Chapter III, Section 1.18 and Proposition 1.19 , DemCADG ] . On overlaps $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v_ i-v_ j)=0$. Taking the Euclidean trace shows that $v_ i-v_ j$ is a harmonic distribution, so it is smooth by elliptic regularity. Choose a smooth locally finite partition of unity $(\chi _ i)$ subordinate to the cover and put $v=\sum _ i\chi _ i v_ i$, each term being extended by zero as a distribution. On the $j$th neighborhood, \[  v-v_ j=\sum _ i\chi _ i(v_ i-v_ j)  \] is smooth. Thus $\beta =T-\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v=-\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v-v_ j)$ is smooth on each neighborhood, hence on $Z$, and it is real and closed. For positive $T$, the same identity expresses $v$ locally as a plurisubharmonic function plus a smooth function. Finally, if $T=\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v=\beta '+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v'$ are two such decompositions, then $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v-v')=\beta '-\beta $ is smooth; taking a smooth Hermitian trace and applying elliptic regularity shows that $v-v'$ is smooth. $\square$

title: Lemma 5.38.5
text:
Lemma 5.38.5 . 65C35F77CB06 Let $Y$ be a connected compact complex manifold. Let $(D_ j)$ be a finite or countable family of distinct prime divisors on $Y$ and $c_ j>0$ real coefficients such that $S=\sum _ jc_ j[D_ j]$ is a positive current of finite mass, and let $ eta $ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $Y$. Let $v\in \mathrm{QPSH}(Y)$ satisfy \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v=S- eta .  \] Then, for $a\in \mathrm{QPSH}(Y)$, the following conditions are equivalent: \[  a\preceq v,\qquad a\preceq _{\mathcal I}v,\qquad 
u (a,D_ j)\geq c_ j\quad \hbox{for every }j.  \] Proof. We first note that $
u (v,D_ j)=c_ j$. Indeed, the restriction of $S$ to $D_ j$ is $c_ j[D_ j]$: distinct divisors intersect in codimension at least two, and such sets carry no mass of any divisor current, also after countable summation. Smooth forms give every divisor zero mass. The local form of Siu's decomposition, applied after a smooth correction, therefore gives $
u (v,D_ j)=c_ j$. Ordinary domination implies ideal domination by proposition 5.33.2 , and ideal domination implies the asserted inequalities for generic Lelong numbers by theorem 5.37.3 . It remains to prove that these inequalities imply ordinary domination. Choose a Hermitian form $\Lambda $ with $a\in \mathrm{PSH}(Y,\Lambda )$. By lemma 5.38.1 and the inequalities $
u (a,D_ j)\geq c_ j$, each finite partial sum of $S$ can be subtracted from $\Lambda +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a$ without losing positivity. Letting the partial sums increase to $S$ gives \[  \Lambda +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a-S\geq 0.  \] Consequently $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(a-v)\geq  eta -\Lambda $. Hence the integrable function $a-v$ has a quasi-plurisubharmonic representative, which is bounded above on the compact manifold $Y$. This yields $a\leq v+C$ almost everywhere, and lemma 5.24.3 extends this inequality everywhere. Thus $a\preceq v$. $\square$

title: Corollary 5.38.6
text: Corollary 5.38.6 . F5277854ECB3 Let $Z$ be a connected compact complex manifold, let $(D_ j)$ be a finite or countable family of distinct prime divisors on $Z$, and let $c_ j>0$. Suppose that $S=\sum _ jc_ j[D_ j]$ is a closed positive current of finite mass. Then there are quasi-plurisubharmonic functions $v$ on $Z$ satisfying \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v=S-\beta  \] for a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $\beta $, and any two such functions differ by a smooth function. In particular, they determine a canonical ordinary singularity type, which depends only on $S$. Proof. Lemma 5.38.4 , applied to $T=S$, gives the decomposition, with $v$ quasi-plurisubharmonic since $S\geq 0$, and shows that any two such potentials differ by a smooth function. By proposition 5.33.1 , they have the same ordinary singularity type. $\square$

title: Lemma 5.38.7
text:
Lemma 5.38.7 . E04E4D6C502E Let $u_ j,u$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on a complex manifold with a common smooth lower curvature bound, that is, $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j\geq - eta $ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\geq - eta $ for one smooth real $(1,1)$-form $ eta $. If $u_ j	o u$ in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$, then at every point $x$, \[  
u (u,x)\geq \limsup _ j
u (u_ j,x).  \] Proof. On a coordinate ball about $x$, add one smooth function to all the potentials to make them plurisubharmonic, and write $p_ j,p$ for the resulting functions. Let $n$ be the dimension and $\kappa $ the Euclidean form of the chart. Distributional convergence gives weak convergence of the positive trace measures $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p_ j\wedge \kappa ^{n-1}$ to $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p\wedge \kappa ^{n-1}$. For every sufficiently small radius $r$ such that the sphere of radius $r$ about $x$ has zero mass for the limit measure, the masses of the balls converge. The Lelong monotonicity formula bounds each $
u (p_ j,x)$ by the normalized trace mass of $p_ j$ on such a ball. Taking the upper limit in $j$, and then letting these radii decrease to zero, gives $\limsup _ j
u (p_ j,x)\leq 
u (p,x)$. Since smooth additions do not change Lelong numbers, this proves the lemma. $\square$

title: Lemma 5.38.8
text: Lemma 5.38.8 . 1792691862B8 Let $Z$ be a connected compact complex manifold and let $\beta $ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form. There is a finite constant $C_\beta $ such that \[  \nu (v,z)\leq C_\beta \qquad \text{for every }v\in \mathrm{PSH}(Z,\beta )\text{ and every }z\in Z.  \] In particular, the generic Lelong numbers of all $v\in \mathrm{PSH}(Z,\beta )$ along all prime divisors are bounded by $C_\beta $. No normalization of the potentials is needed. Proof. Since adding a constant does not change Lelong numbers, we may assume that $\sup _ Zv=0$. By theorem 5.25.2 , these normalized potentials have a common $L^1$ bound. Cover $Z$ by finitely many triples of concentric coordinate balls, a smaller, an intermediate and a larger one, such that the smaller balls cover $Z$. On each larger ball choose a fixed smooth quadratic function $r$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}r\geq \beta $, so that $p=v+r$ is plurisubharmonic there. The functions $p$ obtained in this way have uniformly bounded local $L^1$ norms. Write $d=\dim Z$ and let $\kappa $ be the Euclidean form in the chart. Choose a nonnegative smooth cutoff $\chi $ supported in the larger ball and equal to one on an intermediate ball. Positivity and distributional integration by parts give \[  \int _{\text{intermediate ball}}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p\wedge \kappa ^{d-1} \leq \int \chi \, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p\wedge \kappa ^{d-1} =\int p\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi \wedge \kappa ^{d-1} \leq C\| p\| _{L^1}.  \] Every point of the smaller ball is the center of a Euclidean ball of a fixed radius contained in the intermediate ball. The local Lelong monotonicity formula, recalled in Proposition 6.7.1 , bounds the Lelong number at this center by a fixed multiple of the trace mass of the intermediate ball. The finite cover gives one bound on $Z$. Since smooth additions and additive constants do not change Lelong numbers, this proves the assertion for the original potentials. $\square$

title: Lemma 5.38.9
text:
Lemma 5.38.9 . 1525C5219E69 For a quasi-plurisubharmonic function $u$ on $X$, every local divisor $E$ over $X$, and every real $m>0$, one has \[  \max \! \left\{ 
u _ E(u)- rac{A_ U(E)}m,0ight\}  \leq  rac1m\operatorname {ord}_ E\mathcal I(mu) \leq 
u _ E(u).  \] Here $\operatorname {ord}_ E\mathcal I(mu)$ is the order along $E$ of the pulled-back ideal. Consequently, if locally $a_ m=m^{-1}\log \sum _ k|f_{m,k}|^2+O(1)$, where the $f_{m,k}$ generate $\mathcal I(mu)$, then $
u _ E(a_ m)	o 
u _ E(u)$ as $m	o \infty $. Proof. The upper estimate follows from the local Bergman lower bound in proposition 5.35.1 : the logarithm of the sum of squared moduli of local generators of $\mathcal I(mu)$, divided by $m$, is at least $u$ up to a locally bounded term. Pulling back and taking generic Lelong numbers along $E$ reverses this inequality. For the lower estimate, take a local generator $f$ of the ideal and set $k=\operatorname {ord}_ E(f\circ \pi )$. Near a generic point of $E$, choose a local coordinate $z_1$ defining $E$. Divisorial removal (lemma 5.38.1 ), after a smooth correction, gives \[  u\circ \pi \leq 
u _ E(u)\log |z_1|^2+C.  \] Shrink around a point where the factors of $f\circ \pi $ and of the Jacobian complementary to the powers of $z_1$ do not vanish. The change-of-variables formula and local integrability of $|f|^2\mathrm{e}^{-mu}$ then require integrability in $z_1$ of \[  |z_1|^{2(k+A_ U(E)-1-m
u _ E(u))}.  \] This implies $k+A_ U(E)>m
u _ E(u)$, and in particular the weaker non-strict lower bound in the statement. Taking the minimum over a finite set of local generators and using that orders are nonnegative proves the lower estimate. Since $
u _ E(a_ m)=m^{-1}\operatorname {ord}_ E\mathcal I(mu)$, the last assertion follows by letting $m	o \infty $. $\square$

title: Lemma 5.38.10
text:
Lemma 5.38.10 . 548A845099FB Let $U$ be a complex manifold of dimension $n$, let $u$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic on $U$, and let $\pi :Y	o U$ be a modification with smooth source. Fix $y\in Y$ and an integer $m\geq 1$. Write $J_\pi $ for the holomorphic Jacobian in local coordinates near $y$. If a nonzero holomorphic germ $g$ at $\pi (y)$ belongs to $\mathcal I(mu)$, then \[  \operatorname {ord}_ y(g\circ \pi ) \geq m
u (u\circ \pi ,y)-n-\operatorname {ord}_ yJ_\pi .  \] Proof. If $n\geq 2$, let $ho :\widetilde Y	o Y$ be the blowup of $y$ and let $E$ be its exceptional divisor. For $n=1$, take $ho $ to be the identity and $E=\{ y\} $. Set $F=\pi \circ ho $ and write $J_ F$ for its local holomorphic Jacobian determinant. Generic orders along $E$ give \[  
u (u\circ F,E)=
u (u\circ \pi ,y),\qquad \operatorname {ord}_ E(g\circ F)=\operatorname {ord}_ y(g\circ \pi ).  \] On a standard blowup chart the Jacobian of $ho $ has order $n-1$ along $E$. The chain rule therefore gives the log discrepancy over $U$ as \[  A_ U(E)=1+\operatorname {ord}_ E J_ F =n+\operatorname {ord}_ yJ_\pi .  \] Since $g\in \mathcal I(mu)$, the order of $g\circ F$ along $E$ is at least the order of this ideal. The lower estimate in lemma 5.38.9 , applied to $F$, therefore proves the inequality. $\square$

title: Lemma 5.38.11
text:
Lemma 5.38.11 . 1D91BF7CA736 Let $v$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic on $X$, and let $a$ have analytic singularities on $X$. If $v\preceq _{\mathcal I}a$, then $v\preceq a$. More precisely, it suffices to assume the finitely many inequalities \[  
u (v\circ \pi ,E)\geq 
u (a\circ \pi ,E)  \] for the prime components $E$ of the divisor obtained by principalizing, on one log resolution $\pi $, the ideal of an analytic presentation of $a$. Proof. Principalize the coherent ideal of an analytic presentation of $a$ by a log resolution $\pi :Y	o X$ with smooth $Y$. In suitable local coordinates $z_1,\ldots ,z_ n$ on $Y$, \[  a\circ \pi =\sum _{i=1}^ r b_ i\log |z_ i|^2+B, \qquad b_ i\geq 0,\qquad B\in L^\infty _{\mathrm{loc}},  \] where $r\leq n$. The finitely many inequalities in the statement give $
u (v\circ \pi ,\{ z_ i=0\} )\geq b_ i$; if $v\preceq _{\mathcal I}a$, these inequalities follow from theorem 5.37.3 . Add a smooth local function to $v\circ \pi $ to make it plurisubharmonic. Divisorial removal for this closed positive complex Hessian shows that \[  v\circ \pi -\sum _ i b_ i\log |z_ i|^2  \] has a quasi-plurisubharmonic representative; here the difference is first interpreted off the divisor, or as a locally integrable distribution. Such a representative is locally bounded above. Since $B$ is locally bounded, $v\circ \pi \leq a\circ \pi +C$ on each relatively compact chart of $Y$, away from the divisor. Since $\pi $ is proper, finitely many such charts cover the inverse image of a smaller coordinate neighborhood in $X$, which makes $C$ uniform there. Push the inequality down off the analytic exceptional set; as quasi-plurisubharmonic functions are determined by their values almost everywhere, it then holds everywhere. Finitely many neighborhoods cover the compact manifold, so $v\leq a+C$ globally. The only input from resolution of singularities is the principalization of a coherent ideal. Divisorial removal is applied to the closed positive complex Hessian obtained after a local smooth correction, so no closed background on $X$ is needed. $\square$

title: Lemma 5.38.12
text:
Lemma 5.38.12 . 3CF548646A75 Let $u,v$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic on $X$, and let $s$ have analytic singularities on $X$. Suppose that $u+v\leq s+O(1)$, and let $U_ m,V_ m$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic functions of analytic types $(1/m,\mathcal I(mu))$ and $(1/m,\mathcal I(mv))$. Then there are numbers $\delta _ m\downarrow 0$ such that \[  U_ m+V_ m\leq (1-\delta _ m)s+O(1) \quad \hbox{for all sufficiently large integers }m.  \] The bounded error may depend on $m$. Proof. If $s$ is bounded, upper bounds for $U_ m$ and $V_ m$ give the assertion with $\delta _ m=1/m$ for $m>1$. Otherwise principalize the ideal of $s$ by a log resolution $\pi :\widetilde X	o X$ with smooth $\widetilde X$. Let $E_ i$ be the components of the resulting divisor, with positive coefficients $c_ i$ in $s\circ \pi $; in local coordinates $z_ i$ defining these components, the singular part of $s\circ \pi $ is $\sum _ i c_ i\log |z_ i|^2$. Set $A_ i=1+\operatorname {ord}_{E_ i}(\operatorname {Jac}\pi )$. The hypothesis and lemma 5.38.9 give \[  
u (U_ m\circ \pi ,E_ i)+
u (V_ m\circ \pi ,E_ i) \geq 
u (u\circ \pi ,E_ i)+
u (v\circ \pi ,E_ i)- rac{2A_ i}{m} \geq c_ i- rac{2A_ i}{m}.  \] Choose a positive integer $N\geq \max _ i2A_ i/c_ i$ and put $\delta _ m=N/m$, which is less than one for large $m$. Then the right-hand side above is at least $(1-\delta _ m)c_ i$. After a smooth local correction, divisorial removal from the positive Hessian of $(U_ m+V_ m)\circ \pi $ shows that \[  (U_ m+V_ m)\circ \pi -(1-\delta _ m)\sum _ i c_ i\log |z_ i|^2  \] has a quasi-plurisubharmonic representative, which is locally bounded above. A finite cover of $\widetilde X$ by charts and descent along the proper map $\pi $, as in the proof of lemma 5.38.11 , therefore give $U_ m+V_ m\leq (1-\delta _ m)s+O(1)$. The bounded constant may depend on $m$. $\square$

title: 5.39 Potential regularity and metric distance
text: A Hölder modulus of continuity of the potential controls the trace mass of a positive current on small balls. Averaging the lengths of segments against this trace measure then bounds the distance of the metric defined by the current on its regular locus. This turns regularity of the potential into a metric estimate without any pointwise bound on the Hessian. Let $U\subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a coordinate domain with Euclidean form $\omega _{\mathrm E}=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}|z|^2$ and Euclidean volume $\mathrm{d}\lambda $. Let $0<\alpha \leq 1$, let $\theta $ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $U$, and let $v\in C^{0,\alpha }(U)$ satisfy $T=\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v\geq 0$. Write $\mu =T\wedge \omega _{\mathrm E}^{n-1}$ for the trace measure of $T$. Theorem 5.39.1 . 230882F1D833 For every open set $V\Subset U$ there are constants $C,r_0>0$ such that 33F399DDA815 5.39.2 \begin{equation}  \mu (B(x,r))\leq C r^{2n-2+\alpha },\qquad x\in V,\quad 0<r<r_0. \end{equation} The total variation of every coefficient measure of $T$ is bounded by a constant multiple of $\mu $. Hence the coefficient measures of $T$ vanish on sets of zero Hausdorff $(2n-2+\alpha )$-measure, and all Lelong numbers of $v$ vanish. The estimate implies neither absolute continuity of $\mu $ nor a pointwise bound for the Hessian of $v$. Suppose in addition that $T$ is a smooth Hermitian form $\eta $ on $U\setminus A$ for a proper analytic subset $A\subset U$. For $x,y\in U\setminus A$, let $d_\eta ^ U(x,y)$ be the infimum of the $\eta $-lengths of piecewise smooth paths in $U\setminus A$ joining $x$ and $y$. Then every point of $U$ has a neighborhood $V\Subset U$ such that, for a constant $C$, A1062D2A5198 5.39.3 \begin{equation}  d_\eta ^ U(x,y)\leq C|x-y|^{\alpha /2},\qquad x,y\in V\setminus A. \end{equation} In particular, all sequences in $V\setminus A$ converging to a given point of $A\cap V$ are Cauchy for $d_\eta ^ U$ and have a common limit in the metric completion. If these local hypotheses hold in charts covering $X$, with a proper analytic subset $A\subset X$ and a Hermitian form $\eta $ on $X\setminus A$, then the metric completion of $X\setminus A$ for its intrinsic $\eta $-distance is compact, and the identity of $X\setminus A$ extends to a continuous surjection of $X$ onto it. The metric $\eta $ is incomplete when $A\ne \varnothing $. Both exponents in ( 5.39.2 ) and ( 5.39.3 ) are sharp. Proof. Choose a nonnegative cutoff function $\chi $ equal to one on $B(x,r)$ and supported in $B(x,2r)$, with second derivatives bounded by $Cr^{-2}$. Positivity and integration by parts, after subtracting the constant $v(x)$ from $v$, give \[  \mu (B(x,r))\leq C_1r^{2n}+C_2r^{2n-2} \operatorname {osc}_{B(x,2r)}v \leq Cr^{2n-2+\alpha }.  \] Here we used that the constant $v(x)$ integrates to zero against $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi \wedge \omega _{\mathrm E}^{n-1}$. The matrix $(a_{ij})$ of Radon–Nikodym derivatives of the coefficient measures with respect to $\mu $ is positive semidefinite almost everywhere, so $|a_{ij}|\leq (a_{ii}+a_{jj})/2$. A ball cover proves the assertion about Hausdorff null sets. After a smooth local correction making $v$ plurisubharmonic, dividing ( 5.39.2 ) by $r^{2n-2}$ shows that all Lelong numbers vanish. For the distance estimate, let $m=2n$ and let $\tau $ be the Euclidean trace of $\eta $. Then $\tau \, \mathrm{d}\lambda \leq C\mu $ on the regular locus and $|\xi |_\eta \leq C\sqrt\tau |\xi |_{\mathrm E}$ for tangent vectors $\xi $. Polar integration bounds the average $\eta $-length of the segments from $x$ to the points of $B(x,R)$ by a constant times $\int _{B(x,R)}\sqrt\tau (\zeta )|\zeta -x|^{1-m}\, \mathrm{d}\lambda (\zeta )$. On a dyadic annulus of radius $s$, the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality and ( 5.39.2 ) bound the contribution to this integral by $Cs^{1-m}s^{m/2}s^{(m-2+\alpha )/2}=Cs^{\alpha /2}$. Summing over the annuli gives the bound $CR^{\alpha /2}$. Now let $x,y\in V\setminus A$, and average the lengths of the broken segments $[x,z]\cup [z,y]$ over $z$ in the ball of radius $|x-y|/2$ about the midpoint of $x$ and $y$. By the preceding bound, some such path has length at most $C|x-y|^{\alpha /2}$. For almost every $z$, both segments avoid $A$: proper analytic sets are locally countable unions of smooth strata of real codimension at least two, and the cones from a fixed regular point over these strata have zero volume. If $V$ is small enough, all these paths stay inside $U$. By this estimate, all regular sequences converging to a point of $A$ have a common limit in the completion, and the identity of the regular locus extends continuously across $A$. By compactness, the image of this extension is the entire completion; different points of $A$ may be identified. A sequence converging to a point of $A$ cannot converge in the metric to a regular point, since $\eta $ is bounded below by a positive multiple of the Euclidean metric on a small closed neighborhood of that point. Hence the metric $\eta $ is incomplete when $A$ is nonempty. Finally, the local model $v=|z|^\alpha +|w|^2$, in coordinates $(z,w)\in \mathbb C\times \mathbb C^{n-1}$, has trace mass of exact order $r^{2n-2+\alpha }$ on balls centered on $\{ z=0\} $, and the distance to $\{ z=0\} $ is of exact order $|z|^{\alpha /2}$; this proves both sharpness claims. In later applications to potentials with logarithmic poles, the theorem is applied to the positive residual current that remains after the divisorial part has been removed. $\square$

title: 5.39.4 Dini moduli and limits of distances
search_title: Dini moduli and limits of distances
text: The annular argument of theorem 5.39.1 also applies to a continuous potential whose modulus of continuity is not a power; what matters is a Dini condition on the square root of the modulus. This gives uniform distance estimates for families whose Hölder constants are not controlled. Keep the coordinate domain $U\subset \mathbb C^ n$ with its Euclidean form $\omega _{\mathrm E}$ and volume $\mathrm{d}\lambda $, but now let $v\in C^0(U)$ and let $\theta $ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form with $T=\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v\geq 0$. On the relatively compact charts under consideration, choose a nondecreasing function $m:(0,r_0)\to [0,+\infty )$ with $m(r)\to 0$ as $r\to 0$ such that \[  |v(x)-v(y)|\leq m(|x-y|),\qquad |x-y|<r_0.  \] Put 06D8010B670C 5.39.5 \begin{equation}  D(r)=r+\int _0^ r\frac{\sqrt{m(t)}}{t}\, \mathrm{d}t. \end{equation} Theorem 5.39.6 . 21429B9E1BF3 Assume that $D(r_0/2)<+\infty $ and that $T$ is a smooth Hermitian form $\eta $ on $U\setminus A$ for a proper analytic subset $A\subset U$. Then every point of $U$ has a neighborhood $V\Subset U$ with constants $C,r_1>0$ such that, for $x,y\in V$, \[  d_\eta ^ U(x,y)\leq C D(8|x-y|), \qquad x,y\notin A,\quad |x-y|<r_1.  \] The constants depend only on the charts and an upper bound for $|\theta |$; the dependence on $v$ enters only through $D$. All sequences in $V\setminus A$ converging to a given point of $A\cap V$ have a common limit in the metric completion. If these hypotheses hold on a finite cover of a compact connected manifold by charts, the metric completion of the regular locus is compact, and the identity of the regular locus extends to a continuous surjection of the manifold onto it. If $A$ is nonempty, the metric $\eta $ on the regular locus is incomplete. Proof. Write $d=2n$ and $\mu =T\wedge \omega _{\mathrm E}^{n-1}$. The same cutoff calculation as in theorem 5.39.1 , with a constant subtracted from $v$, gives \[  \mu (B(x,s))\leq C\bigl (s^ d+s^{d-2}m(2s)\bigr ).  \] This uses only the bound for $\theta $; closedness of $\theta $ is not needed. If $\tau $ is the Euclidean trace of $\eta $, then $\tau \, \mathrm{d}\lambda \leq C\mu $ on the regular locus. Polar integration bounds the average length of the segments from a regular point $x$ to the points of $B(x,R)$ by \[  C\int _{B(x,R)}\sqrt{\tau (\zeta )} |\zeta -x|^{1-d}\, \mathrm{d}\lambda (\zeta ).  \] On an annulus of outer radius $s$, the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality and the trace bound make the contribution to this integral at most \[  Cs^{1-d}s^{d/2} \bigl (s^ d+s^{d-2}m(2s)\bigr )^{1/2} \leq C\bigl (s+\sqrt{m(2s)}\bigr ).  \] For $s_ j=2^{-j}R$, monotonicity gives \[  \sum _{j\geq 0}\sqrt{m(2s_ j)} \leq \frac1{\log 2}\int _0^{4R}\frac{\sqrt{m(t)}}t\, \mathrm{d}t.  \] Indeed, $\sqrt{m(2s_ j)}\log 2$ is at most the integral of $\sqrt{m(t)}/t$ over $[2s_ j,4s_ j]$, and these intervals have disjoint interiors; no doubling condition on $m$ is needed. The average length is therefore at most $CD(4R)$. For $x,y\in V\setminus A$, average the lengths of the broken segments $[x,z]\cup [z,y]$ over $z$ in the ball of radius $|x-y|/2$ about the midpoint of $x$ and $y$, applying the preceding bound with $R=2|x-y|$ at each endpoint. Since the volume of this ball is comparable to $R^ d$, some broken path has length at most $CD(8|x-y|)$. As in the proof of theorem 5.39.1 , almost every such path avoids $A$, and for small $V$ it stays inside $U$. Since $D(r_0/2)<+\infty $, we have $D(r)\to 0$ as $r\to 0$. Hence any two regular sequences converging to the same point are Cauchy and have the same limit in the completion. The argument for the completion in the proof of theorem 5.39.1 applies with this modulus. A positive lower bound for $\eta $ near a regular point prevents a sequence converging to a point of $A$ from converging in the metric to the regular point. This also proves incompleteness when $A$ is nonempty. $\square$ Corollary 5.39.7 . 380EB17A4350 In the setting of theorem 5.39.6 , let $V$ be as in the theorem. For $0<\beta \leq 1$, a modulus $m(r)\leq Cr^\beta $ gives $d_\eta ^ U(x,y)\leq C'|x-y|^{\beta /2}$ for sufficiently close $x,y\in V\setminus A$. If instead \[  m(r)\leq C(-\log r)^{-a},\qquad a>2,  \] then for sufficiently close $x,y\in V\setminus A$, \[  d_\eta ^ U(x,y)\leq C'(-\log |x-y|)^{1-a/2}.  \] These are only sufficient conditions; we do not claim that the Dini condition is necessary. Proof. Integrating the square root of the power modulus gives a multiple of $r^{\beta /2}$. For the logarithmic modulus, the substitution $s=-\log t$ gives \[  \int _0^ r\frac{(-\log t)^{-a/2}}t\, \mathrm{d}t =\frac{(-\log r)^{1-a/2}}{a/2-1}.  \] In either case the term $r$ in $D(r)$ is bounded by the asserted rate for small $r$. The theorem now gives both estimates; the fixed dilation of the argument of $D$ changes only the constants. $\square$ Corollary 5.39.8 . D3B517FBCE4F Let $\omega _0$ be a Hermitian form on $X$ and $d_{\omega _0}$ the distance of the associated Riemannian metric. For each $j$, let $T_ j=\theta _ j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j\geq 0$, where $\theta _ j$ is a smooth real $(1,1)$-form, $v_ j$ is continuous, and $T_ j$ is a smooth Hermitian form off a proper analytic subset $A_ j$. Assume \[  |\theta _ j|_{\omega _0}\leq \Lambda ,\qquad |v_ j(x)-v_ j(y)|\leq m(d_{\omega _0}(x,y)),  \] with one fixed $\Lambda $ and one nondecreasing modulus $m$ tending to zero such that the function in ( 5.39.5 ) satisfies $D(r_0/2)<+\infty $. By theorem 5.39.6 , the identity of $X\setminus A_ j$ extends to a continuous surjection of $X$ onto the metric completion of $X\setminus A_ j$; let $d_ j$ be the pseudometric on $X$ obtained by pulling back the completed distance. Then the diameters of the $d_ j$ are uniformly bounded, and a subsequence converges uniformly on $X\times X$ to a continuous pseudometric. If $T_ j\geq c\omega _0$ on the regular loci for one $c>0$, the limit is a metric and dominates $\sqrt c\, d_{\omega _0}$. Proof. A finite fixed chart cover and the theorem give common constants $C,r_1>0$ such that \[  d_ j(x,y)\leq CD(Cd_{\omega _0}(x,y)), \qquad d_{\omega _0}(x,y)<r_1.  \] For a pair meeting $A_ j$, approximate it by regular pairs in the manifold topology. The completed distance and $D$ are continuous, so the same estimate holds for all such pairs in $X\times X$. No uniform bound on the geometry of the analytic sets enters the constants. Dividing a minimizing geodesic of $d_{\omega _0}$ into a uniformly bounded number of short pieces and using the triangle inequality gives a uniform diameter bound. The triangle inequality also gives \[  |d_ j(x,y)-d_ j(x',y')| \leq d_ j(x,x')+d_ j(y,y'),  \] so the distance functions are equicontinuous. The Arzelà–Ascoli theorem gives a subsequence $d_{j_ k}$ converging uniformly on $X\times X$ to a function $d_\infty $. Nonnegativity, symmetry, vanishing on the diagonal and the triangle inequality pass to the limit. The lower bound $T_ j\geq c\omega _0$ gives $d_ j\geq \sqrt c\, d_{\omega _0}$, first for regular pairs and then for all pairs, which proves the last assertion. Without this lower bound the limit may degenerate. For $\varepsilon _ j\downarrow 0$, take $\theta _ j=\varepsilon _ j\omega _0$ and $v_ j=0$, with $A_ j=\varnothing $. These data satisfy the hypotheses with $m(r)=r^2$, and $d_ j=\sqrt{\varepsilon _ j}\, d_{\omega _0}$ converges uniformly to zero. $\square$
